item.title: JJ Redick goes off on the Lakers' bench after almost blowing the lead against the Raptors
item.description: JJ Redick goes off on the Lakers' bench after almost blowing the lead against the Raptors originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Lakers had one of their best performances of their 2026-27 season so far against the Toronto Raptors. They went up by as much as 26 points and led by 16 points in the final two minutes of the game. This prompted Lakers head coach JJ Redick to clear out his bench to see out the game. Unfortunately, the bench unit did not live up to expectations, as they almost blew the lead. This led to Redick sending Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves, Walker Kessler, and Matisse Thybulle back in to see out the game and get the 131-125 win. JJ Redick admits he is disappointed by the Lakers' bench after almost blowing the game It is normal for coaches to send in their bench players to see out a game, especially when they have a lead as big as 16 points. However, what the Lakers' bench players showed against the Raptors was a bad sign, which is why Redick is putting his foot down. He does not like what happened in the game against the Raptors, especially since he wanted to rest his starters. Unfortunately for the Lakers, Redick had to send the starters back in because he wanted to secure the win rather than give up the massive lead in just a couple of minutes. MORE: JJ Redick speaks on what it's like seeing Luka Doncic dominate up close Thankfully for Redick and the Lakers, the starters were stable enough to get the result. It was a big win for the Lakers, but it does show some bad signs if the mediocre bench performances continue, which could have a long-term effect on the players and the coaching staff's approach to games. "I won’t make that mistake again. I’ll leave the guys in. You got to play to the final buzzer," Redick said about sending his bench in after getting a 16-point lead . It will be a big lesson for the Lakers moving forward, not only for Redick, but also for the players. When they are playing with a massive lead late into the game, the players must learn how to deal with the pressure and close out the win. It should never be stepping off the gas, they just need to balance their aggression with some semblance of control to get the win without any issue. item.title: Collin Sexton emerging as a valuable piece of the Lakers' rotation
item.description: Nov 1, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers guard Collin Sexton (10) moves the ball against the Toronto Raptors during the second half at Crypto.com Arena. LOS ANGELES — The Los Angeles Lakers have never been short on star power, but building a championship-caliber roster requires more than just elite talent at the top of the rotation. It takes players who embrace their roles, bring energy when their number is called, and provide a different dimension to the team's identity. That is exactly what the Lakers hope to get from Collin Sexton. After signing a two-year, $19.2 million contract this past summer, Sexton arrived in Los Angeles as an important addition to the team's second unit, expected to provide scoring, toughness, and another reliable ball handler behind Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves. Nov 1, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77) reacts with guard Collin Sexton (10) against the Toronto Raptors during the second half at Crypto.com Arena. Jonathan Hui-Imagn Images Nov 1, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77) reacts with guard Collin Sexton (10) against the Toronto Raptors during the second half at Crypto.com Arena. Seven games into his Lakers tenure, Sexton is still finding his rhythm in a new environment. However, there have already been glimpses of what he can bring to a roster loaded with star talent. Sunday night provided another example. Sexton finished with 14 points, three rebounds, and three assists in 19 minutes, shooting an efficient 6-of-10 from the field as the Lakers secured their fifth victory of the season, defeating the Raptors 131-125 to improve to 5-2. His ability to make an impact without needing an abundance of minutes is something the Lakers will need throughout a long regular season, particularly with the expectations surrounding this group. Through seven games, Sexton is averaging 8.9 points, 1.9 rebounds, and 1.9 assists while shooting 26.9% from beyond the arc. Although his three-point shooting has yet to find consistency, his scoring instincts and aggressive approach remain evident. Earlier in the week, Sexton delivered perhaps his most impressive performance in a Lakers uniform, erupting for 21 points in just 21 minutes off the bench against the Los Angeles Clippers. Oct 28, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers guard Collin Sexton (10) reacts after a basket in the second half against the Los Angeles Clippers at Intuit Dome. Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Oct 28, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers guard Collin Sexton (10) reacts after a basket in the second half against the Los Angeles Clippers at Intuit Dome. That performance offered a reminder of the offensive firepower he can provide when he gets into a rhythm. item.title: How will Wales fare on Nations Championship return?
item.description: Wales have won three Tests under head coach Steve Tandy [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Wales will start their international season next weekend when they return to the Nations Championship. Steve Tandy's side face four games as they host Japan, New Zealand and Australia in Cardiff, before a final play-off match at the Allianz Stadium completes the November schedule. The autumn games begin the road to the 2027 World Cup in Australia in a year's time. BBC Sport Wales provides a recap of what has happened so far in the inaugural running of the global tournament and looks at what lies in wait over the next month. What is the Nations Championship? The Nations Championship pits the northern hemisphere teams who compete in the Six Nations - England, Ireland, Scotland, Wales, France and Italy - against southern hemisphere giants South Africa, New Zealand, Australia and Argentina, plus invited sides Fiji and Japan. All teams play each of the six nations in the opposing hemisphere once, with three rounds of fixtures having already been staged in July and now another three in November. Their results will rank the teams within their own hemisphere, from one to six, before a final play-off weekend at the Allianz Stadium in Twickenham. Where are Wales internationals really made? Wales counting down the year until World Cup How have Wales fared so far and who do they play next? Wales will resume the Nations Championship in fifth place in the northern hemisphere standings after a mixed July campaign. It started with an encouraging six-try victory against Fiji at the Cardiff City Stadium, which was considered a home venue for the Pacific Islanders side. But Wales faltered during a demanding travelling schedule as they were outclassed by Argentina in San Juan and thrashed by South Africa in Durban. Now they face a trio of home games in Cardiff with the opening match staged against Eddie Jones' Japan side, who also sit fifth in their table, with the two teams potentially meeting twice this November. The tests will become harder when Dave Rennie brings his New Zealand side to Cardiff on 14 November, before the Wallabies arrive seven days later. Results so far Saturday, 4 July: Fiji 24-39 Wales Saturday, 11 July: Argentina 35-21 Wales Saturday, 18 July: South Africa 43-0 Wales Remaining fixtures Saturday, 7 November: Wales v Japan, Principality Stadium, Cardiff, 16:40 GMT Saturday, 14 November: Wales v New Zealand, Principality Stadium, Cardiff, 14:10 GMT Saturday, 21 November: Wales v Australia, Principality Stadium, Cardiff, 20:10 GMT. Who is in the Wales squad this autumn? Uncapped Dragons duo Aneurin Owen and Che Hope, and Cardiff prop Rhys Barrett were named in a 39-strong group for the November Tests, with hooker Dewi Lake again handed the captaincy. Head coach Tandy called up Dragons lock Seb Davies and Cardiff number eight Taine Basham for the first time since he took charge of the national side in September 2025. item.title: Eagles vs. Commanders: The good, the bad, and the ugly
item.description: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 01: Stefon Diggs #3 of the Washington Commanders scores a touchdown reception against Kenny Moore II #23 of the Philadelphia Eagles during the second quarter at Northwest Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the last six days, the Eagles’ checkout line has quadrupled. Apathy has arrived on November 1st after the Eagles lost their sixth-straight game, stumbling against the previously one-win Washington Commanders, 27-10, at Northwest Stadium on Sunday night. The last time the Eagles lost six-straight games was in 2012, Andy Reid’s last season that ended in a 4-12 finish. Right now, the Eagles, who are 2-6, can only wish that they might win four games this season. It’s where teams that give up go. Yes, the Eagles are that bad (but lately can be used as a great sedative) . Here, it said the Eagles season was through after the 25-14 loss to Carolina in Week 6. Many believe that sentiment now. The Eagles are in sole possession of last place in the NFC East at 2-6, behind 2-4-1 Washington, 3-5 Dallas and the 4-2-1 New York Giants. After Rachaad White’s clinching touchdown with 1:52 left to play, chants of “Eagles suck, Eagles suck,” were heard throughout Northwest Stadium. Who could argue? The Eagles played as complete a game as a lowly, lifeless, capitulating team can. They were awful in all three phases: special teams, defense and offense. In the second half, the Eagles averaged an NFL-low 5.3 yards and 111 yards of offense entering the game managed to even sink below that against Washington, getting shutout in the second half and gaining 155 yards, blown up by cosmetic plays in the last minute. Tanner McKee continues to look skittish in the pocket, on the run, in pretty much anything he does. He was sacked five times for minus-35 yards, completed 23 of 34 for 212 yards with an interception. Washington rushed for 135 yards, making the Eagles the only team in the NFL since 1968 to allow 100 or more rushing yards through the first eight games of the season. Because the Eagles cannot stop the run, defensive coordinator Vic Fangio has been forced to reconfigure his defensive structure, bringing the back end closer to the line of scrimmage. Because Fangio has had to rotate up help in the box, the Eagles are sacrificing deeper areas of the field. The Commanders had plays of 14, 18, 20, 21 (2), 30, 33 and 53 yards. It was Washington’s first comeback win this year, rebounding from a 10-0 deficit. The Eagles cannot pick up a blitz. They cannot handle overloads on one side or the other. They are unable to push the ball downfield. They have the second-longest losing streak in the NFL, behind the winless Los Angeles Chargers. What is even more frustrating, to the fanbase at least, is that the team does not seem to care as they sink. item.title: Wolff hits back at critics after title win: "This is Kimi Antonelli!"
item.description: Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff could not hide his satisfaction with Kimi Antonelli 's historic title win at the Mexico City GP, yet again pointing to the naysayers that claimed the Italian was too young for F1 . Antonelli's P3 finish at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, behind fellow champions Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton, respectively, was more than enough to secure a historic F1 Drivers' title. The 20-year-old has now beaten former Red Bull driver Sebastian Vettel’s age record - achieved at the Abu Dhabi GP in 2010 - by three years and 66 days to become F1’s youngest ever title winner. Speaking briefly to Sky Sports amidst the celebrations in Mexico City, Wolff said: "[People asked] Why do you put this kid in the car? Oh, it's Kimi Antonelli. THIS is Kimi Antonelli! Incredible. Also today, completely serene. That's what makes him so different." Wolff later appeared again with the broadcaster, going into further detail on why he was right to back the young Italian. “We have to pinch ourselves because it seems like yesterday he was 11 years old in a garage in junior karting and it goes so fast. “He wins the junior formulas, then a difficult year in F2 and that's already where people start outside started to doubt. Then when Lewis told me he was going to Ferrari, it was my immediate reaction that we’ve got to put him in the car." Wolff proud after Antonelli proves doubters wrong Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Wolff even revealed sponsors left Mercedes upon Antonelli's promotion but despite knowing the "calculated risk" of handing a then 18-year-old Antonelli his debut in 2025, the Austrian expressed his pride in backing the Italian. “But people doubted. We had two sponsors leaving us because of that, because of ‘who is this kid?’ There were others who stayed with us until today. Some are here that reaped the full reward. “And then the difficult year and people said again, he shouldn't even be in Formula 1 or he should be at a smaller team. Over nine races, no points, the tears in Spa and then this. “I'm just so proud for the team that all of them continue to trust him and he delivered. It was instinctive. Lewis left. I called Bradley and said, Kimi is in the car next year. We knew the data, so it kind of felt the right thing to do. I think it was always a calculated risk, not a real risk.”

item.title: Mauricio Pochettino has a USMNT roster dilemma, and the 2028 Olympics are making it more complicated
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino’s U.S. roster announcement for the first official matches since the World Cup is days away, but beyond decisions common before every international window, he must also sort out whether his young prospects belong with the first team or the junior platoon with Olympic medal aspirations. Starting Nov. 9, the squads will gather separately — Pochettino’s for the CONCACAF Nations League’s quarterfinals against Haiti and Steve Cherundolo’s under-23s for a head start on the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Had Pochettino not invited a dozen newcomers to senior camp six weeks ago, the intrigue this week wouldn’t rise above a typical selection. During victories over Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada, however, several showed they were up to the challenge. In all likelihood, many will join Cherundolo for what is expected to be an overseas camp and friendlies. Cherundolo worked with Pochettino’s staff at the last camp, and the two coaches are collaborating on this week’s selections. With greater public attention on an Olympics at home, the U.S. Soccer Federation has placed extra emphasis on building a strong team. (Olympic men’s soccer is restricted to players 23 and under, with three overage exceptions.) Cherundolo will conduct additional camps in many of the international windows over the next 18 months. Christian Pulisic celebrates his fourth-minute goal in AC Milan's 3-1 win over Inter Milan on Saturday. NurPhoto via Getty Images At the moment, Pochettino might need to peel off a few players for this camp at the national training center in the Atlanta area, followed by games against Haiti on Nov. 14 in Miami and Nov. 17 in Cincinnati. (The U.S. has never failed to advance to the final four.) The frontline sits at the forefront of Pochettino’s decisions. After missing the September-October call-up to recover from injuries, top strikers Folarin Balogun and Ricardo Pepi scored over the weekend as second-half subs for Monaco and PSV Eindhoven, respectively. (Pepi also assisted during the 7-0 romp over Willem II.) It was the first goal since the World Cup’s round of 32 for Balogun, who has played just 116 minutes in Ligue 1 for Monaco. Pepi returned Saturday after missing six weeks with a muscular injury. Both are involved in European competition this week: Eindhoven hosts Club Brugge on Wednesday in the Champions League and Monaco faces Nordsjaelland on Thursday in the third-tier Conference League. Christian Pulisic, whose injury recovery and limited playing time at AC Milan kept him out of the previous U.S. camp, scored the opening goal four minutes into a 3-1 win over rival Inter Milan on Saturday. Pulisic and Milan are back at it Thursday against Ferencvaros in the second-tier Europa League. item.title: itel Energy offers 48-hour repairs, product replacement to customers at exhibition
item.description: itel Energy, a clean energy and power solutions brand, has promised to repair or replace faulty solar power equipment within 48 hours for customers across Nigeria as part of its after-sales support. The company reemphasized their commitment during the Nigeria Energy exhibition week in Lagos, where it showcased new products and showed distributors, installers, both new and existing customers how its after-sales service works. The company said it offers remote services, home visits and product replacement where necessary. According to the company, after-sales service is an important consideration for households and businesses switching from petrol and diesel generators to solar power, because a faulty inverter or battery can disrupt electricity supply and business operations. Speaking on the sidelines at the exhibition, the Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder of SunFi, a major distributor of itel Energy products, Rotimi Thomas, said the commitment boosted customers’ confidence in the products distributed through the company. “The 48-hour resolution commitment from itel Energy is very important for us as a distribution platform because we don’t make the product and when a consumer buys a product through SunFi, they’re actually really buying a trusted service,” Thomas said. He explained that customers needed assurance that equipment would be repaired or replaced when problems arose, rather than being left to deal with faults after purchase. “That trust comes from the type of equipment that we use and the promise of being able to replace or repair the assets when there’s a problem,” he said. Thomas also urged customers to look beyond warranty periods when choosing solar equipment, saying the speed and quality of support during the warranty period were equally important. “But even more important than that five-year warranty is what happens before the five years or during the five-year period. How do you respond when I report that I have a problem with the product now?” Thomas said the cost of solar systems remained a barrier to adoption, adding that the company offers instalment payment plans for households and businesses unable to pay the full amount. According to him, about 30 to 40 per cent of prospective customers still request payment plans, which shows the need for financing options that make clean energy more accessible. He said some customers preferred to pay between 10 and 30 per cent upfront and spread the balance over three, six, 12 or 24 months, or longer. Meanwhile, itel Energy’s Country Service Manager, Emmanuel Kumuyi, said most common complaints reported by customers included overloading, protection issues and incorrect installation. He said some problems arose when solar panels, inverters and batteries were not properly matched to the user’s power requirements. item.title: How to Watch Illinois vs. Nebraska: Game Time, TV Channel, Online Streaming and Odds
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, IL - OCTOBER 24: Illinois Fighting Illini head coach Bret Bielema looks on during the college football game between the Oregon Ducks and the Illinois Fighting Illini on October 24, 2026, at Gies Memorial Stadium in Champaign, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Allio/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images How to Watch Illinois vs. Nebraska Game Time: 7 p.m. Friday TV Channel: FOX Online Streaming: FOX ONE Odds: ILL +6.5, O/U 48.5 Quick Hits: Illinois Fighting Illini (5-3, 3-2 Big Ten) Head Coach: Bret Bielema (6th season) 9-4 in 2025, 5-4 in conference Last Game: Illinois 20, Maryland 17 Nebraska Cornhuskers (5-3, 2-3 Big Ten) Head coach: Matt Rhule (4th season) Last Game: Washington 17, Nebraska 10 What Happened the Last Time These Two Teams Played? All-time series tied 2-2. S ept. 20, 2024: Illinois 31, Nebraska 24 LINCOLN, Neb. — The cardiac Illini pulled off an improbable upset, this time in overtime fashion on the road in a sold-out crowd, against a No. 22 Nebraska, 31-24. In a top-25 Big Ten conference matchup under the Friday night lights, Illinois quarterback Luke Altmyer and the Illini outplayed star Nebraska freshman quarterback Dylan Raiola and the Cornhuskers. It was a back-and-forth game all night. After a five-plus minute drive Nebraska — with its backup kicker in the game — would miss a 39-yard effort to set up a game-winning drive opportunity for Illinois. It ultimately led to overtime. Altmyer delivered in overtime as he threw a touchdown on the first drive to wide receiver Pat Bryant. The Illinois defense then held up its end of the bargain, sacking Raiola twice to force a three-and-out 40 yards from the line of scrimmage en route to the victory. The Illinois (4-0, 1-0 Big Ten) offense looked poised all night. Altmyer in particular had another impressive performance going 21-of-27, four touchdowns, and again zero interceptions. Altmyer’s most impressive stat was a 78% completion percentage. For most of the night, a poised Raiola led the way for Nebraska (3-1, 0-1 Big Ten), as he finished regulation with 284 yards and 3 touchdowns through the air. Illinois opened the game doing exactly what it needed to do if they wanted to win: set the tone with an opening drive touchdown. While Illinois has a wide variety of flavors in the running back room, the backs have struggled to put up big numbers in the trenches. That trend continued tonight as the Illinois running back room only combined for 166 yards.

item.title: “We Want More” Has An Increasingly Hollow Ring For Sunderland
item.description: COVENTRY, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 31: Omar Alderete of Sunderland receives a red card after receiving a second yellow card from referee Simon Hooper during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Coventry City and Sunderland at The Coventry Building Society Arena on October 31, 2026 in Coventry, England. (Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Saturday evening, as we sifted through the wreckage and tried to make sense of Sunderland’s dismal defeat at the hands of Coventry City, I would’ve quite happily loaded the words “meltdown”, “bedwetting” and “headloss” into a cannon, lit the fuse and blasted them into outer space. Halloween horror stories are nothing new, but this was an effort straight from the George A.Romero school of brutality and the latest horrific result to which Sunderland’s fans have been subjected. In classic splattercore fashion, the Lads ran straight towards the danger in the Midlands, looked entirely unprepared for what was coming, and were duly picked off. Nine points were on offer from our three most recent league outings, and we banked a total of one. Not good enough. Nowhere near. And yet, even as recently as last week, when a dour 0-0 home draw with Leeds was being hailed in some circles as a step forward (I’m sorry, but effort should not be praised unless it’s something truly exceptional), there was still a belief that the corner would be turned and that from somewhere, we’d find the solution. It hasn’t been — and we haven’t. Denial is not a viable option here. Blithely claiming that “It’ll click” is foolish. Flagging up ropey metrics and claiming that the picture isn’t as stark as it appears to be is borderline insulting. Domestically, Sunderland have been mediocre for the bulk of the season, and it’s showing no signs of changing. The issues of responsibility and accountability must be addressed if we’re to have even the slightest chance of getting out of this mess. And to that end, the focus must be placed upon the players, coaches and higher-ups whose actions (and occasionally inaction, it must be said), and decisions have landed us in a relegation battle that few might’ve seen coming but that we must all accept. Currently looking worryingly short of ideas and showing no signs of changing his approach, Régis Le Bris is carrying the can for Sunderland’s ills and to a point, that’s fair, but make no mistake: those around him shouldn’t escape scrutiny — least of all Florent Ghisolfi, whose maiden solo flight and forays into the transfer market didn’t yield the results needed. He worked brilliantly alongside Kristjaan Speakman in order to build a competitive top flight side for 2025/2026, but the jury remains firmly out on too many of his most recent additions, and even those that’ve shown promise aren’t being trusted enough. Legitimate concerns about Sunderland’s style of play, our form, our lack of defensive solidity, midfield cohesion and attacking spark have been flagged up for weeks. Pundits and analysts w

item.title: Marcus Rashford is ready to leave Man United in January on one condition
item.description: Marcus Rashford is ready to leave Man United in January on one condition Manchester United forward Marcus Rashford’s career has gone haywire in the past two years. The English forward, who rose through the ranks at Carrington, was once considered the future of the club. After scoring 30 goals and registering 12 assists under former manager Erik ten Hag in the 2022/23 season, it was believed that Rashford would usher in a new era of dominance at the Theatre of Dreams. Unfortunately, he failed to hold on to that form, Ten Hag lost his job, and Ruben Amorim’s arrival marked a dark chapter in the academy graduate’s career. The Portuguese head coach was soon at daggers drawn with the academy graduate, who was offloaded to Aston Villa and then Barcelona on loan deals. The Englishman was expected to leave permanently this summer, but the Catalans performed a U-turn and Michael Carrick decided to take a bet on the player. Unfortunately, Rashford is yet to justify the English manager’s trust. Rashford’s season so far With United needing a new left-forward and Rashford failing to find a suitor, it appeared as though the stars had aligned to rekindle an old partnership this summer. The Englishman started the season in the left-forward role, failed to impress, and has since dropped down the pecking order. Rashford has appeared eight times in all competitions for the Red Devils this season, six of which have been starts, and he is yet to register a goal or an assist. The player is currently sidelined with an injury, but could return to the squad this week. Rashford by season (2022/23–2026/27) Recent reports suggest that Everton are eyeing a move for the Englishman in January and United are ready to let him leave at the turn of the year. A fresh update regarding the 29-year-old’s stance on an exit from the Theatre of Dreams has now emerged. Rashford will consider exit if he fails to secure regular minutes According to Football Insider , Rashford could consider his future this summer if he is no longer a first-team regular at Old Trafford. The report states: “Marcus Rashford could explore a move away from Manchester United if he is not playing regularly, sources have told Football Insider.” Speaking on The Football Insider podcast, journalist Pete O’Rourke added: “It’s maybe not worked out so far, but I think in Rashford’s defence he he’s been carrying a bit of an injury since the World Cup.Carrick would love to have a fit and firing Marcus Rashford because he would definitely be an improvement for that Manchester United attack.” “But it’s a difficult one for Rashford because he really had his heart set on that move to Barcelona and for it to fall through was a big blow to him, now he’s come back to United.” “For Rashford, if he’s not playing regularly and he finds himself sort of on the fringes at Old Trafford, then maybe he might have to seek a move away to another club.He did it before, when he went on loan to Aston Villa and then he went on loan to Barcelon

item.title: Sunderland Must Find Answers Fast – Or Face the Consequences
item.description: SUNDERLAND, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 25: Regis Le Bris, Manager of Sunderland portrait on the bench before during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Sunderland and Leeds United at Stadium of Light on October 25, 2026 in Sunderland, England. (Photo by Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images) | Getty Images The message to the Sunderland squad is very clear: sort your shit out. Stop letting each other down. One fact remains for Régis Le Bris’ side that should offer some comfort: the team is playing so far within themselves that it almost defies belief. Where is what made them the group they were last season, and why has it disappeared? It is a club where various areas are letting themselves down when they don’t have to. Petulance, disconnect, tactical confusion, and meek surrender are the cornerstones of this football club right now – in the league, at least. A team that cannot defend and doesn’t take its chances. A team that is set up in a way that doesn’t have a proper shape or wingers. Brian Brobbey up front can look alarmingly isolated. Players whose body language has fluctuated between committed and disgracefully complacent. Did we not learn anything from last season? If not, then the lesson bears repeating: nothing comes easily in this division. It felt like we had to have the pedal pressed to the metal just to reach 40 points. It was hard. Very hard. Yes, there is the relative success in the cup competitions, but that feels very much like Alan Partridge’s still-good news about the chocolate oranges. It is not what he will be judged by. Of course, there are mitigating factors – injuries and the World Cup haven’t helped at all – but they will affect all sides in the Premier League. Sunderland are not unique in that regard. Can Le Bris survive? Given the fixtures coming up, it would seem unlikely, particularly alongside the track record of the board. Sadly, prior achievements rarely outweigh the urgent business of survival. Just ask Claudio Ranieri at Leicester a decade ago. If he does go, it would be devastating, because we have so much to thank him for. But given the possible repercussions of failing to make a change, it might be that his position is untenable, unless Sunderland get two victories in the next four games. The only thing which will save Le Bris is proving he has the answers. Yet that process should have begun against Coventry, but there was no response whatsoever. If there is one thing we know, it is what relegation looks like. This is not a squad of 2002/03 or 2005/06, but it could well be one of 1996/97. This is a side more than good enough to stay up, but the team needs to seriously interrogate what they want from themselves and the professional pride they need to display. Something is not right; what exactly, no one knows except those on the inside of the club. Nor do we know the solutions. But my advice to Régis Le Bris would be to ensure your mind is as open as possible. Play those who are doing well – Ahoka, Ta

item.title: OTD (02/11/1972): Sunderland Reacts And Wonders What’s Next
item.description: Alan Brown, Sunderland manager July 1969 (Photo by PA Images via Getty Images) | PA Images via Getty Images It was the day after the loss of an institution at Sunderland, as a meeting at Roker Park the previous day ended with the club parting company with manager Alana Brown “by mutual agreement”. Brown walked out of Roker Park immediately after a meeting with Sunderland directors, including chairman Keith Collings, without saying goodbye to the players. But a day had gone by, and Brown was tracked down at his home by journalists and had given his reaction: I’ve been in this game much too long for anything to come as a surprise. I feel no bitterness towards anyone. In fact I shall continue to be a Sunderland supporter. I always have been, ever since I was a toddler. I shall go to watch them play whenever I can. I still believe that the club can be one of the forces in the game within five years. They have so many talented young players if only they are allowed time to develop. I shan’t have any personal contact with them now. Not that I don’t want to but I think it would be unfair to whoever takes over to interfere with him in any way. I still think I have a lot left to give the game. There’s no fitter man than me in the game today. There’s no rush but I’ll start looking around eventually. I have no desire to go round stabbing anyone in the back because of what has happened today. I don’t want to know what the directors have said in their statement. That is entirely a matter for them. My only immediate thought is that I am sorry to have to leave behind what I still consider to be a fine bunch of players. For what it is worth, I thought when I went to the ground today that it might be for the final time. But I really didn’t think about it a great deal. There were a lot of other things to be getting on with. I think you can safely say that my association with the club is over once and for all. If you look at my history you will see that I don’t go anywhere more than twice. That’s what my life is these days, I don’t know in what capacity. I have no thoughts about whether it will be another manager’s job or coaching or something else. I have nothing fixed up for the immediate future. The chairman had not made himself available for comment, but in a short statement, the club said: At a meeting this morning it was unanimously agreed that Mr. Alan Brown’s contract be terminated forthwith. No decision has been made as to his successor and this will be discussed at tomorrow’s board meeting. Brown’s contract was due to expire at the end of the season and were reported to be £250,000 in debt and losing £2,000 a week and the previous week, three new directors joined the Roker Park board, a move described by Mr. Collings as “the first stage in putting the club in order.” What’s Next? item.title: Editorial: Sunderland Are in Trouble – But How Did It Get This Bad?
item.description: COVENTRY, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 31: Regis Le Bris, Manager of Sunderland, reacts during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Coventry City and Sunderland at The Coventry Building Society Arena on October 31, 2026 in Coventry, England. (Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, I wrote my last editorial on 12th October, which you can read here , and I explained my worries about how things were going then. It’s now three weeks down the road, and we’re in big trouble. Bottom of the Premier League table after a quarter of the season has gone, four points behind Coventry in 16th, with only one side in the league having scored fewer goals (Forest in 19th) and only one having conceded more (Palace in 18th). Like I said, we’re right in the sh*t. Our last three games against Bournemouth, Leeds and Coventry were a chance to turn our season around – and we took one point from a possible nine. Looking at our next five league games, I just don’t know where the points will come from if the Sunderland from last season doesn’t turn up soon. For too many weeks now, we’ve been saying we expect a reaction in the next game, but time and again, it hasn’t happened. At some point, you simply run out of next games – one way or another. The reaction of the players and the manager after the goalless draw against Leeds was that we’d turned a corner, but that was all relative when compared to the dross served up in the majority of games in the Premier League so far. The way I see the season so far is that we turned up in the first half at Brentford, then at home to Arsenal and away at Pep-less City. And that’s it for me. Two-and-a-half games out of nine where I reckon we’ve turned up with the same commitment with which we approached most of last season. At the moment, we’re in danger of throwing the last two years of progress down the lav, where they end up as one of our many “what if?” moments, rather than a fundamental long-term reset of Sunderland’s place within football’s hierarchy in England and in Europe. But how the f**k did we get here…? (And feel free to add to it, because there’s bound to be something I’ve missed.) Recruitment… Qualifying for the Europa League should have been an opportunity to attract the next level of player to add real quality to the squad. But, in summary, we made two major signings for a combined total of around £60m, and they have started one game between them in the Premier League. One. Out of a possible total of 18 between them. What is the situation with Fofana and Methalie?! Does Le Bris just not fancy them? Did Ghisolfi want us to play a different way and the manager isn’t on the same page? Are they not settling? Are they not fit enough? Or did Le Bris and Ghisolfi agree they’d bring them in but not play them in the Premier League for a while? item.title: Fan Letters: Sunderland Fans Have Their Say – Is Régis Le Bris’ Time Up?
item.description: SUNDERLAND, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 25: Sunderland head caoch, Regis Le Bris looks on during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Sunderland and Leeds United at Stadium of Light on October 25, 2026 in Sunderland, England. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) | Getty Images Dear Roker Report, I wrote in after the Bournemouth game, stating that the club was in crisis and that there were no discernible positives to be found in recent performances. I also noted that while Le Bris should be given the right to fix this, it must happen immediately. I have since ‘given my head a wobble’ and ‘considered where we were a few years ago’, as suggested by some of the predictable comments in response, and I can’t say I’ve changed my opinion. On the contrary, I have become more convinced, after another league game where we created nothing, literally nothing, from open play, and made another bang-average side look like the World XI from EAFC Kick-Off mode, that if we want to remain a Premier League side next season, things must change, and change now. I say this with a heavy heart, as Régis Le Bris has little competition for the best Sunderland manager I can remember in my lifetime (29). However, eras have endings, manager/club relationships have shelf lives, and the evidence of our eyes and ears cannot continue to be ignored. Last season’s rock-solid defence looks like a bunch of strangers, the previously dynamic and exciting midfield looks like a group of Championship players, and the forward line looks almost as toothless as the average attendee of the Gallowgate. If Le Bris were to go now, he’ll be forever remembered as the man who took Sunderland back into the Premier League and into the seemingly impossible heights of Europe. If he stays, he’ll also be the man who takes us down. Matthew Laidlaw Dear Roker Report, Yet again, we bottle it at Coventry. First and foremost, Ahoka should be in the team. We rocked up and showed fuck all. Alderete, hang your head in shame. You are dog shit. Régis, instead of picking the same players that served us well last year, change the fucking team up now and again. Please get a centre-forward, otherwise we are relegated. Talbi should be starting instead of Angulo. Relegation fodder yet again, and yet again we will set the record for the lowest points gained in the Premier League. Very fucking frustrated with today’s performance. Wake up before it’s too late. The football club should give those unfortunate supporters who travelled down to that piss-poor show their money back. item.title: NBA fans have mixed reactions to Scottie Barnes and Luka Doncic's scuffle during Lakers vs Raptors
item.description: Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images Luka Doncic and Scottie Barnes were involved in a little altercation during the Los Angeles Lakers’ win over the Toronto Raptors. The Lakers superstar dominated the game and led them to a very impressive 131-125 win in Los Angeles on Sunday night, but the Raptors did what they could to get under his skin. At one point in the game, Barnes and Doncic got into a scuffle, and that seems to have divided NBA fans over whose fault it actually was. NBA fans react to Luka Doncic and Scottie Barnes’ scuffle during Lakers vs Raptors At first glance, it looked like it was Barnes trying to tangle arms with Doncic, and many felt that the former should’ve been penalised for that. However, several others on the internet have pointed the finger at the Lakers star for his role in the scuffle. One fan tweeted: “How is that a double foul? Dude is trying to walk, and Scottie is wrapping his arm up.” Another wrote: “How do you call a foul on Luka there? “You can blatantly see Scottie tangling arms with Luka,” said another. One fan with an opposing stance said: “I hate when Luka does this. Man up and fight through the contact, man.” Another reacted by saying: “No way Luka is crying about this.” “This is what Yaxel was talking about. Watch Luka looking at the referee,” wrote another. Fans can pick sides between Barnes and Doncic all they like, but it’s the latter who had the last laugh with a fantastic performance. Doncic scored 45 points, while recording 15 rebounds, six assists and five steals. He was easily the best player on the court and was the reason why the Lakers won the game. The Lakers are now 5-2 this season, while the Raptors are stuck at 3-3. item.title: Dolphins’ Malik Willis gives honest assessment of Patriots’ defense after Week 8 loss
item.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Dolphins’ Malik Willis gives honest assessment of Patriots’ defense after Week 8 loss appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Malik Willis got real on how the New England defense kept him and the Miami offense in check following the Dolphins’ 24-19 loss to the Patriots on Sunday evening. Willis is halfway through the fifth season of his NFL career, his first with the Dolphins. This marks his first year as a full-time starter, being a key leader in Miami’s rebuilding offense. Miami is going through a brutal start to the season, finally getting their first win after beating the New York Jets. However, they returned to the loss column after falling to the Patriots. Willis reflected on the loss after the game, per reporter Joe Schad. He gave props to the New England defense for playing more man-to-man coverage than zone coverage, limiting the options Miami had on offense. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I think they did a good job. All credit to the defense, all credit to the Patriots. We just got to continue to figure out what we’re going to do as far as adjustments go, as far as how we want to attack different schemes,” Willis said. How Malik Willis, Dolphins played against Patriots Malik Willis and the Dolphins have a lot of work to do in their rebuild. Learning how to manage adjustments from opponents like what the Patriots did to them will be one of those lessons. Miami initially had the upper hand over New England, taking a 13-3 lead at halftime. However, the Patriots roared back with a 21-6 display in the last 30 minutes of regulation. Willis had a decent display leading Miami’s offense before New England contained him in the second half. He completed 21 out of 32 passes for 211 yards and two touchdowns and one interception. Ollie Gordon II was the standout in the run game, racking up 19 carries for 69 yards. Kevin Coleman Jr. led receivers with 46 yards and a touchdown on three catches. Greg Dulcih and Caleb Douglas both had four receptions for 43 yards, while Malik Washington caught five passes for 40 yards and a touchdown. The Dolphins look to bounce back in their next home matchup. They host the Detroit Lions as kickoff commences on Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 2, 2026
item.description: The naira’s exchange rate against the US dollar remains a major focus for businesses, importers, investors and Nigerians who depend on foreign currency for international transactions. The Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the parallel market are two major segments of Nigeria’s foreign exchange market, with rates varying according to currency supply, demand and market conditions. As of Monday, November 2, 2026, the latest available figures indicate that the official NFEM rate stood at ₦1,346.26 per dollar, while the parallel market quoted the dollar at approximately ₦1,386.36. Official NFEM exchange rate Data published by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) showed that the naira traded at an average rate of ₦1,346.2565 per dollar on Friday, October 30, the latest available official trading data ahead of Monday’s session. The official market also recorded a closing rate of ₦1,346.00 per dollar, reflecting a marginal improvement from the previous trading session. The NFEM rate is determined by the volume-weighted average of transactions in the official foreign exchange market. It serves as the benchmark for official foreign currency transactions in Nigeria. Central Bank of Nigeria Dollar to naira black market rate today In the parallel market, commonly known as the black market, currency dealers quoted the dollar at approximately ₦1,380.59 for buying and ₦1,386.36 for selling as of Sunday, November 1. This means Nigerians seeking to purchase one dollar from parallel market operators would need approximately ₦1,386, although the actual amount may vary depending on the dealer and location. The parallel market rates are indicative and may change throughout the day in response to foreign exchange demand and supply. Difference between official and parallel market rates The difference between the latest official NFEM weighted average of ₦1,346.26 and the parallel market selling rate of ₦1,386.36 is approximately ₦40.10 per dollar. The gap reflects differences in foreign exchange supply, demand and pricing across the two markets. For individuals and businesses purchasing dollars, the parallel market selling rate remains an important consideration, particularly for transactions that cannot be processed through official banking channels. How much is $100 in naira today? At the latest available official NFEM rate of ₦1,346.26, $100 is equivalent to approximately ₦134,626. At the parallel market selling rate of ₦1,386.36, $100 would cost approximately ₦138,636. These figures are indicative and do not necessarily represent the final rates offered by banks or individual currency dealers. Nigerians are advised to confirm prevailing exchange rates with their banks or licensed Bureau de Change operators before conducting foreign exchange transactions. item.title: Broncos Will ‘Do Everything in Their Power’ for RB Trade: Report
item.description: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks at the scoreboard during the second quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) Getty The Denver Broncos may have just gotten what seemed like a breakout performance from rookie running back Jonah Coleman in a 28-24 win over the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 8 — but it’s important to remember that all of this is relative. According to DNVR’s Zac Stevens, the Broncos are still very much going after Indianapolis Colts running back and NFL All-Pro Jonathan Taylor, no matter how great Coleman looked on Sunday. “I believe the Broncos are going to do everything in their power to trade for Jonathan Taylor,” Stevens said on Sunday night. “This could happen at any moment. You might not want to go to sleep Broncos Country. The Broncos are going to try to pull this trade off, from my understanding. They want Jonathan Taylor now.” ESPN’s Adam Schefter and NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport previously named the Broncos as one of the teams circling a trade for Taylor. Schefter and Rapoport reported that the Broncos, Green Bay Packers , Seattle Seahawks , and Minnesota Vikings are chasing Taylor. The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones added the New York Giants to the list of “possible suitors.” “The Green Bay Packers, Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos and Vikings are among the teams that have pondered, or are expected to consider, the possibility of a trade for the star running back, according to sources,” Schefter and Rapoport wrote on October 25. The price for Taylor, reportedly, is similar to what the San Francisco 49ers gave up when they obtained running back Christian McCaffrey from the Carolina Panthers in 2022 — a 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th-round pick. Jonathan Taylor: Elite RB on Terrible Team Taylor, 5-foot-10 and 226 pounds, has toiled as one of the NFL’s elite running backs on one of the league’s worst teams and worst-run franchises since the Colts drafted him in the 2nd round (No. 41 overall) of the 2020 NFL Draft after a record-setting career at Wisconsin. As a rookie, Taylor rushed for 1,169 yards and 11 touchdowns in 15 games before leading the NFL in rushing yards and touchdowns in 2021 with 1,851 yards and 18 touchdowns. After two injury-riddled seasons in 2022 and 2023, Taylor bounced back in a big way, rushing for 1,431 yards and 11 touchdowns in 2024 and 1,585 yards and 18 rushing touchdowns in 2025. item.title: Rams Head Coach Sean McVay Hilariously Says He Will ‘Crush’ Aaron Donald
item.description: Head coach Sean McVay accepted blame for the Los Angeles Rams losing to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1. Getty The Los Angeles Rams scored a much-needed victory over the lowly Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday and head coach Sean McVay was in better spirits than he’s been for much of what has been a pretty disappointing season. He was able. to laugh and joke about his star defensive lineman Aaron Donald who made a pretty embarrassing blunder during the game. Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert lost control of the football as he was scrambling on one play deep in his own territory and Donald, the 35-year-old future Hall of Fame inductee, tried to track down the ball and would have had an easy scoop and score had he come up with it cleanly but he didn’t get a good grasp on it, kicked it a bit, and the ball ended up going out of bounds which meant that the Chargers retained possession of the ball when the Rams should have had prime field position at the very worst. McVay was asked about the play after the game and he said the following: “Aw man, I’m going to give him such a hard time about that. I mean, I saw what he was thinking because it’s going right in front of you and he’s thinking, ‘I’m going to scoop and score,’ and he knocks that [expletive] out of bounds, I mean, what the [expletive]. So, his face he couldn’t even look at me and make eye contact after that.” He also reportedly said, “I’m gonna crush him for that,” per J.B. Long. Rams could use some laughs amidst rough start to the season It was a much-needed win which brings the Rams to 4-4 on the season. Many analysts predicted they would be a superteam at the start of the season but perhaps those expectations were far too lofty as the team has looked rather pedestrian at best and just downright bad at certain times throughout the campaign so the fact they were able to take care of business against a bad opponent is good news for the Rams. An optimist would look at their situation and feel pretty good about things. Their next two games should be wins on paper as they will play the Washington Commanders and Arizona Cardinals, although they did lose to Arizona at home earlier this season, before their bye week in Week 11. They are still without Myles Garrett so if they can get him and some of their other injured players back for a late season run and are able to enter the playoffs with some momentum, even if they don’t end up winning the NFC West, then they will still be a team that no one in the NFC wants to face. That funny Donald moment may be a nice little bit of levity for McVay who can certainly run hot at times. There hasn’t been much to laugh about this season so moments like that matter just to ease the pressure a little bit. item.title: Nolan Traore lifts Nets to first win of season with big second half
item.description: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images Nolan Traore lifts Nets to first win of season with big second half appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Brooklyn Nets needed a lift on Sunday against the shorthanded Indiana Pacers as they sought their first win of the season. Sophomore point guard Nolan Traore answered the call. After an ugly first half in which the Nets scored 43 points on 15-of-39 shooting (38.5 percent), Traore sparked the offense. The French Floor general scored a team-high 14 points and drained four threes during the second half, lifting Brooklyn to a 98-90 victory. He finished the game with six assists and one turnover. “The difference was just us moving the ball well and trying to find the best shot every time, and also being consistent on defense. That’s the main thing,” Traore said. “I think [the difference for me] was just like great spacing. I know that they want to double Julius [Randle], so we take advantage of this. And we made shots also. We did a great job. I’m happy and proud of my teammates.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) yessirr NT https://t.co/SjBgLtMmW3 pic.twitter.com/M9ggY3tPiN — Brooklyn Nets (@BrooklynNets) November 2, 2026 General Manager Sean Marks has said he is “looking for the next Nets.” Traore is among the team’s most promising young prospects, alongside Egor Demin and Mikel Brown Jr. After adding noticeable muscle this offseason, the 20-year-old has impressed. He’s averaged 14.3 points on .467/.389/.727 shooting splits, with 4.0 assists and 2.0 turnovers per game across his last four outings. Traore has started the Nets’ last three games. Brooklyn was without Demin (right leg contusion) and Brown (back injury management) on Sunday. Nets grind out ugly victory over Pacers on back of Nolan Traore’s big second half Robert Goddin-Imagn Images Michael Porter Jr. led the Nets with 23 points, nine rebounds and three assists in the victory, while Julius Randle added 20 points, five rebounds and six assists. The duo combined for 12-of-31 shooting while turning the ball over eight times. They know that won’t be enough in coming games, but they did enough down the stretch Sunday to pick up a much-needed victory. “It wasn’t a pretty win, but it’s a win regardless. We got that zero out of that column, so we’re really happy about that,” Porter said. “If you’re going to be a good team, eventually you’ve got to learn how to win games like this. item.title: Commanders add to Eagles’ 2026 misery with huge Week 8 SNF win
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Commanders add to Eagles’ 2026 misery with huge Week 8 SNF win appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Eagles hit a new low Sunday night , falling 27-10 to the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium. What started as a promising evening quickly morphed into a nightmarish collapse, extending Philadelphia’s agonizing losing streak to six games. Early on, Philadelphia looked like it would control the Sunday Night Football matchup. Running back Saquon Barkley capped a quick drive with a three-yard touchdown run after kicker Jake Elliott got the team on the board with a 40-yard field goal, staking the visiting squad to a 10-0 lead. That initial spark vanished rapidly. Washington ripped off 27 unanswered points to blow the contest wide open. Rookie kicker Drew Stevens spearheaded the comeback by drilling four consecutive field goals, while quarterback Jayden Daniels connected with wide receiver Stefon Diggs for an eight-yard touchdown pass to knot the game before halftime. Daniels finished the night completing 16 of 29 passes for 217 yards and a touchdown, with wide receiver Treylon Burks hauling in a 53-yard bomb to set up key points. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Philadelphia backup quarterback Tanner McKee, filling in under heavy pressure, struggled to establish any rhythm. McKee completed 23 of 34 passes for 212 yards but suffered five sacks and coughed up two costly turnovers. Edge rusher Dorance Armstrong Jr. delivered the game’s turning point with a strip-sack on McKee that set up a Washington field goal. Defensive back Rasul Douglas later sealed Philadelphia’s fate by picking off McKee’s fourth-and-25 prayer late in the fourth quarter. Running back Rachaad White punched in a one-yard touchdown run on the next play to cap the scoring. Unforced errors proved fatal for Philadelphia. An illegal formation penalty negated a successful field goal in the second half, and Elliott subsequently pulled the retry wide. The 2-6 Eagles now face a mountain of questions as their season spirals out of control. Can head coach Nick Sirianni turn this around before it’s too late? item.title: Former Canadiens Draft Target Flipped to Western Rival
item.description: MONTREAL, CANADA - MAY 25: Head coach Martin St. Louis of the Montréal Canadiens reacts after the 3-2 overtime loss against the Carolina Hurricanes in Game Three of the Eastern Conference Final of the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs at Bell Centre on May 25, 2026 in Montreal, Quebec, Canada. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty When the Montreal Canadiens won the 2022 NHL Draft Lottery, the prevailing assumption in many NHL circles was that they were going to select forward Shane Wright with the first overall pick. However, they selected Juraj Slafkovsky instead, who has gone on to become one of their core pieces; Wright eventually was taken by the Seattle Kraken, and has largely underwhelmed so far in his NHL career. But now, he’ll have a new opportunity to succeed elsewhere, as he was traded on Sunday to the Nashville Predators. Former Montreal Canadiens Draft Target Shane Wright Traded To The Predators From The Kraken Getty SEATTLE, WASHINGTON – FEBRUARY 28: Shane Wright #51 of the Seattle Kraken skates against the Vancouver Canucks during the second period at Climate Pledge Arena on February 28, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. TRADE ALERT 🚨 Former first-round picks Shane Wright and Matthew Wood are on the move after a one-for-one swap! pic.twitter.com/8XfOjSJ467 — NHL (@NHL) November 1, 2026 So far this season, Wright has scored three goals with one assist in 14 games played, a pace of 18 goals and six assists over a full 84-game season. In the 183 games he’s skated in during his NHL career, which has been spent exclusively with the Kraken, Wright has scored 39 goals with 43 assists for 82 points with 34 penalty minutes, a plus-15 rating, and has averaged 13:42 of ice time per game. Wright, who is signed through the end of the 2026-27 NHL season, carries a salary cap hit of $886,666. Shane Wright Was Linked To The Canadiens Before They Went In A Different Direction Wright was one of the top prospects heading into the 2022 NHL Draft, and many expected the Canadiens to take him with the first overall selection; it was also the first time since the Habs selected Doug Wickenheiser in 1980 that they held the first overall pick. Instead, Montreal selected Juraj Slafkovsky, while Wright fell to No. 4, where the Seattle Kraken chose him. Wright’s reaction while walking past the Canadiens’ draft table became one of the biggest moments of the night, as cameras caught him giving the team’s management a memorable glare. Since then, Wright’s NHL numbers haven’t lived up to the expectations that came with being viewed as a potential first-overall pick. This article was originally published

item.title: Stipe Miocic Recalls UFC 241 Eye Injury While Praising Tom Aspinall for Vacating Heavyweight Title
item.description: The UFC heavyweight division has been left in a difficult spot since Tom Aspinall vacated his undisputed title in September. The Englishman announced on social media that another injury to his right eye during training had disrupted his recovery, leaving his return timeline uncertain. Aspinall hasn’t competed since October 2025, when his heavyweight title fight against Ciryl Gane ended in a no-contest following a series of eye pokes. The 32-year-old later revealed that he had already agreed to a date for his next fight before suffering another setback involving the same eye. Unfortunately, the latest injury means he will have to spend even more time away from the Octagon. The Englishman was originally expected to headline UFC 334 against Gane in a heavyweight title unification bout. However, his latest injury forced the promotion to change its plans. Gane has since been elevated to undisputed champion and is now scheduled to defend the belt against Josh Hokit. As for Aspinall, his next major update is expected to come in January 2027, when he revisits his doctor for another assessment. If the eye hasn’t recovered as hoped, he could require another operation. That would mark his third surgery on the right eye and fourth overall. Amid the uncertainty, former two-time heavyweight champion Stipe Miocic has praised Aspinall for making the difficult decision to vacate his title rather than keep the division waiting. Stipe Miocic Backs Tom Aspinall’s Heavyweight Title Exit For Full Recovery Speaking to Casino.org, Miocic shared his thoughts on the situation and said, “Looking at Tommy’s situation, I just think, ‘Good of him to do that. I understand it’s probably hard for him to vacate his title the way he did. I give him kudos for doing that because I know it’s hard for him.” Miocic also related to Aspinall’s situation, having dealt with his own eye injury following an accidental poke from Daniel Cormier at UFC 241 . That night, Miocic knocked out the Hall of Famer to reclaim the heavyweight championship he had lost at UFC 226. Reflecting on the experience, he added, “He was on top of the world, and then everything changed. He got an eye poke. I’ve been there. I’ve torn my retina before, and it’s tough. I just want to give him lots of credit for doing that.” The former champion then recalled how the injury affected him after his second fight with Cormier. He said, “It happened to me in my second fight with DC (Cormier). I got poked in the eye accidentally, and after the fight, I was kind of like, ‘Man, my eyes are kind of weird-looking and feeling weird.’ Unfortunately, these things happen, but he just has to move on from it and just see it as bad luck.” Miocic also had a message for the UFC, suggesting that Aspinall shouldn’t worry about the promotion’s reaction to his decision. item.title: Rams’ Sean McVay not on the same page as LA president when it comes to Chargers rivalry
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Rams’ Sean McVay not on the same page as LA president when it comes to Chargers rivalry appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Rams took care of business against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, but Sean McVay and team president Kevin Demoff apparently have very different views on the crosstown matchup. After the Rams’ 24-9 win at SoFi Stadium , McVay was asked whether he considers the Chargers a rival. His answer was short and to the point. “Kevin Demoff does. I don’t,” McVay said, via Gary Klein of the Los Angeles Times. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Demoff, for his part, did not hide his excitement about the result. The Rams president celebrated on X with a GIF of Will Ferrell’s Ron Burgundy from “Anchorman” saying, “That’s amazing,” which ESPN’s Adam Schefter later shared. McVay’s comments are not surprising. The Rams and Chargers have both called Los Angeles home since relocating about a decade ago and now share SoFi Stadium, but they rarely see each other. The NFL schedule pairs the two teams only about once every four years, and Sunday’s game was just their second meeting since the stadium opened in 2020. Their facilities are also far apart, with the Rams practicing in the western San Fernando Valley and the Chargers based more than 30 miles away in El Segundo. McVay also made it clear before the game that he was not overlooking the winless Chargers. “I really couldn’t care less what the record says,” McVay said last week . “I see a team that’s really good. They’ve had a chance to win a lot of these games.” The Chargers made it a game for a half. They led 9-3 behind three Cameron Dicker field goals before Kyren Williams punched in a 1-yard touchdown run late in the second quarter to give Los Angeles a 10-9 halftime lead. The Rams took over from there. Blake Corum broke free for a 23-yard touchdown run early in the third quarter, and Matthew Stafford found Puka Nacua for an 18-yard score to make it 24-9. The defense did the rest, intercepting the Chargers twice and recording two sacks while holding them scoreless after halftime. The win improved the Rams to 4-4 and gave them their second straight victory. The Chargers, meanwhile, remain winless . Whether McVay calls it a rivalry or not, the Rams now hold an 8-6 edge in the all-time series. They will visit the Washington Commanders next Sunday. Related: Rams’ secondary takes major hit with Trent McDuffie, Jaylen Watson injuries vs Chargers Related: Ian Rapoport’s Myles Garrett injury update brings ‘optimism’

item.title: Eagles get wrecked by Commanders in epic meltdown: Nick Sirianni is on hot seat— what happens next?
item.description: LANDOVER, Md. — The Eagles have expressed confidence that they could dig themselves out of a 2-5 hole to save their season, but the team shouldn’t believe that anymore. It’s over. The Eagles dropped their sixth consecutive game on Sunday night in a 27-10 loss to the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium. Now, the 2-6 Eagles have the worst record in the NFC East and have almost no shot of making the playoffs. The Eagles are one of the NFL’s worst teams. In a few months, the organization could make major changes during the offseason to get the team back on track. Will Eagles coach Nick Sirianni escape this nightmare season? It’s going to be tough. If the Eagles continue to play this poorly, the team could move in another direction after the season. Sirianni is squarely on the hot seat. Here are NJ.com’s takeaways from the Eagles’ 17-point loss vs. the Commanders: Eagles’ defense is leaky The concern heading into Week 8 was Philadelphia’s defense would spiral after giving up 38 points to the Cowboys last week and collapse down the stretch. That could end up happening. In the second quarter, Commanders wide receiver Stefon Diggs capped off an 11-play, 89-yard drive by reeling in an eight-yard touchdown over Eagles safety Kenny Moore. Moore gave up the touchdown because he was flat-footed in coverage. On Washington’s final scoring drive of the first half, the Eagles left Diggs wide open on a crossing route, and he racked up 20 yards on the catch-and-run to Philadelphia’s 30-yard line. Washington kicked a field goal on that drive, but Washington’s offense could have caused more damage. Daniels missed a touchdown throw to Okonkwo, who was wide open near the 20-yard line. With 2:51 remaining in the third quarter, Eagles All-Pro cornerback Quinyon Mitchell was beaten downfield by Treylon Burks on a 53-yard catch to Philadelphia’s seven-yard line. Philadelphia’s defense struggled for most of the game, but it had some good moments, too, including making a third-down stop from the seven-yard line to hold Washington to a field goal. With 5:34 remaining in the first quarter, second-year Eagles safety Drew Mukuba knocked the ball out of Commanders tight end Chigoziem Okonkwo’s hands for a fumble, and it was recovered by Eagles linebacker Zack Baun at Washington’s 26-yard line. Four plays later, the Eagles scored their first touchdown of the game. Some progress, but the Eagles’ offense is still bad For the second consecutive week, the Eagles showed some promise on offense, but the product still wasn’t very good. Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee completed 23 of 34 passes for 212 yards. He also threw an interception. The Eagles only finished with 91 rushing yards. Star running back Saquon Barkley was not explosive because he played through back and hamstring injuries. He finished with 13 carries for 30 yards. item.title: Wales not finished product but all roads lead to 2029
item.description: Wales won four matches in 2026, three more than in 2025 [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Head coach Sean Lynn admits Wales are far from the finished product but says he has been hugely encouraged by their WXV showings. An eight-try mauling of South Africa in Cardiff and two Test wins out in Japan saw Wales finish World Rugby's new Global Series on a high. Only a narrow two-point defeat by USA - a team ranked in the world's top six - prevented a clean sweep. It marks quite the transformation for Lynn's side who had been on a nine-Test losing streak prior to the tournament and slumped to an all-time low world ranking of 13th. "Twelve months ago we didn't win a game in the World Cup. We've worked so hard as a group of players and staff and we've come into this WXV with three out of four wins," said Lynn. "Are we the finished product? No we're not, but we're seeing the bigger picture of that roadmap to the 2029 World Cup. "There are areas that we need to be looking at and the players now need to go back to the PWR [Premiership Women's Rugby] and Celtic Challenge because we're still looking to move that dial. "But I can't fault the effort from players and staff, it's been a really intense 11 weeks." Lynn hails grit of 13-player Wales in Japan win Wales complete Japan double to end WXV on a high Young talent shines through Wales' transformation began with a brutal pre-season during which Lynn secured the permanent services of assistant coaches Ashley Beck and Steve Salvin. That, along with Tyrone Holmes' growing impact as defence coach and the introduction of strength and conditioning specialist Gareth Harris, gave Wales some much-needed stability. "We've all been really specific about what we want to do. We've established a DNA and I'm really proud of all the hard work - physical and mental - that not just the players have put in, but also the staff," said Wales co-captain Kate Williams. "It's competitive within the team and that's showing on the pitch as well against other teams." Lynn has capped 12 new players during his 18 months in charge and in doing so has unearthed gems such as Seren Lockwood, Branwen Metcalfe, Freya Bell and Amy Williams. "It's super important that we are always watching. Amy Williams for instance, what I saw of her at Cardiff Met and Brython Thunder, I really liked," he said. "She's very brave, likes to get the ball in her hands and always wants to beat that first defender. Individuals like her and Freya Bell have been like ducks to water coming into the international arena and I believe there are more out there. "The senior players are now having that competitive edge in the squad, and they know that the jersey is not theirs." Lynn has shown he is not afraid to make big selection calls and has backed the youngsters all summer, with the first glimpse of his new-look side coming in the 34-17 victory over Barbarians . item.title: Uninspired LAFC drops regular season home finale to Minnesota United FC
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- There was an opportunity on Sunday evening for LAFC to gain three important points as they push for a top four finish in the Western Conference. Doing so would provide home-field advantage in the opening round, best-of-three series of the MLS Cup Playoffs. Instead, they put forth a lackluster effort, falling 3-1 to Minnesota United FC at BMO Stadium. It was Minnesota's first victory against the Black & Gold in Los Angeles since 2019. LA finished with a 9-4-4 record in their 17 home games this season, with one final match remaining on the road before postseason play begins. "I am responsible. I am not happy," interim head coach Xavi Tamarit said. "All of us, we are very disappointed with this game...we want to say sorry to the people who were in the stadium, who were watching us on the TV, because this is not the team we want to show." LAFC got off to a slow start from the beginning, stringing together a disorganized attack and failing to generate any real chances through the opening 30 minutes. The defense held firm for most of that stretch, holding Minnesota without a shot attempt through its first 28 minutes. Midfielder Joaquín Pereyra, with his squad's first attempt of the match, made it a 1-0 game in favor of the visitors in minute 29. He took advantage of a well-placed throw-in from defender Cherrion Valerius, which dropped down perfectly in front of Pereyra as he rocketed his shot past Hugo Lloris. Minnesota United FC midfielder Joaquín Pereyra (26) smiles during the first half of an MLS soccer match against LAFC at BMO Stadium, Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026, in Los Angeles. Ruben Ibarra II - The Sporting Tribune Minnesota United FC midfielder Joaquín Pereyra (26) smiles during the first half of an MLS soccer match against LAFC at BMO Stadium, Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026, in Los Angeles. Valerius kept the momentum rolling in Minnesota's favor, adding a score of his own just five minutes later. He used his run to meet a header from forward Kelvin Yeboah and volley it over the top of Lloris to make the score 2-0. This was beautiful from @MNUFC 👏 Cherrion Valerius scores on the assist from Kelvin Yeboah to make it 2-0. pic.twitter.com/CEyHbtoTfF — Major League Soccer (@MLS) November 2, 2026 The second half was no different. LAFC continued to look stagnant and impatient. Their runs came across as forced, and the quality of chances did not get any better until the late stages. Denis Bouanga, Son Heung-min and the rest of the attack simply lacked the composure and cohesiveness to turn their luck around and claw back. There would be no repeat of the 2-0 lead that they erased last Sunday against the LA Galaxy. Pereyra scored the dagger goal in the 81st minute to earn himself a brace, drilling a left-footed strike from distance that Lloris could not get to in time with his diving attempt. It’s not every day that a rugged football player gets honest about mental health. That’s why it’s heartwarming to hear Oliver be vulnerable and show his appreciation to his friends on the team for all they’ve done for him during these difficult times.
