item.title: Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg joins Wilt Chamberlain club after career night vs. Clippers
item.description: Justine Willard-Imagn Images Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg joins Wilt Chamberlain club after career night vs. Clippers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg is already finding his name next to some of the greatest players in franchise history after a monster night against the Los Angeles Clippers . The first-year forward erupted for a career-high 37 points in Golden State’s 124-112 win on Sunday night at Chase Center. Lendeborg was nearly unstoppable, shooting 13-of-19 from the field, 6-of-11 from three and 5-of-6 from the free-throw line while adding six assists, four rebounds and a steal in 34 minutes. According to ESPN Insights , it was the most points by a Warriors rookie in a game since Stephen Curry dropped 42 in 2010. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The big night also pushed Lendeborg into rare company. He is now averaging 22.3 points per game, making him just the third player in franchise history to average at least 20 points over his first seven career games. The only others to do it are Hall of Famers Wilt Chamberlain , who averaged 37.4 points in 1959-60, and Rick Barry, who put up 22.9 in 1965-66. Lendeborg’s performance was even more impressive considering the circumstances . The Warriors played without both Curry and Draymond Green, leaving the rookie to shoulder much of the scoring load. It was also a major bounce-back effort. Lendeborg struggled in Friday’s win over the Los Angeles Lakers , finishing with six points and five turnovers before fouling out in 24 minutes. “I had no impact on the game whatsoever (on Friday), and then the depth came in, and they took care of everything,” Lendeborg told reporters . He had plenty of help on Sunday, too. De’Anthony Melton added 21 points on six 3-pointers, while Brandin Podziemski and Brandon Williams each chipped in 17. Golden State shot 53.5% from the field and knocked down 22 threes. Rui Hachimura led the Clippers with 24 points, and Kobe Sanders added 16. The Warriors selected Lendeborg with the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft out of Michigan, where he averaged 15.1 points and 6.8 rebounds last season. Some viewed his age as a drawback, as he entered the league at 24, but the Summer League MVP has been a polished contributor from day one . The win was Golden State’s fourth straight, improving the Warriors to 4-3 after an 0-3 start. They will look to keep the momentum going when they host the Phoenix Suns on Monday. Related: Warriors’ Yaxel Lendeborg advocates for ‘ethical hoops’ after career night Related: Warriors’ Steve Kerr shares eye-opening reaction to Yaxel Lendeborg’s 37-point night

item.title: Struggling Slavia face Arsenal as grim record looms
item.description: Slavia have failed to win any of their last 22 Champions League games (Michal Cizek) Hosting Arsenal in the Champions League on Wednesday, Slavia Prague are facing the mammoth task of ending a drawn-out winless streak in the competition as an unwelcome record looms. The Czech champions have won a single game out of 23 in the Champions League -- on their debut in the competition against Steaua Bucharest in September 2007. They have since only managed eight draws and 14 losses over four Champions League campaigns including the current one. "Of course the longer it gets, the more unpleasant it is," said Jindrich Trpisovsky, the Slavia manager since 2017. "The streak is long and as we keep talking about it, I brood over it more than in the past," he added. Record holders AEK Athens failed to win 24 straight games from 1992-2006, while Steaua, now known as FCSB, recorded 23 winless games between 2006 and 2013. Slavia host Arsenal fresh off the back of their 1-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield, which would daunt most teams, before Villarreal at home and Bayern Munich away in their next European games. "Of course we know how tough European games are and how hard you must work to win," said Trpisovsky. "In some games we were on the front foot and we got beaten. This is the beauty of football." - 'Unlucky' - Slavia have faced Arsenal three times in the Champions League, recording a draw and two losses including a humiliating 7-0 drubbing in London in 2007. "Slavia simply face the best teams whose quality is obvious," said Vladimir Smicer, a former Slavia striker who won the Champions League with Liverpool in 2005. "I think they were unlucky a few times," he told AFP. Slavia were close to breaking the hoodoo in this year's opener against Lens -- reduced to 10 men, they took a 2-1 lead in the 89th minute but squandered the chance and lost 3-2. "That's bad luck really. But the streak is unpleasant in any case," said Smicer, who played for Lens from 1996-1999. "And they are now facing teams like Arsenal and Bayern and these are games you don't expect Slavia to win." Smicer said Slavia should rather have beaten lower-ranked teams like Sabah to whom they lost 2-0 in Baku in October. "Slavia has a deep roster so the coach can adapt to the playing style of their opponents, but in the end it's all about quality," he added. "In Baku they simply underperformed, like in some other games, and that extended the winless streak. There have been games they should have won but unfortunately it didn't happen." Slavia will host Arsenal on November 4, exactly a year after losing 3-0 to the Gunners in the Champions League at home. Slavia defender David Zima hailed the competition as "a football university". "It's the top level and you can't stress out about having to win now. This is simply football and you can't always win. You just need a little luck." Bo Nix expressed amazement toward the atmosphere of the home crowd following the Denver Broncos’ remarkable win over the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday evening. Nix is halfway through the third season of his budding NFL career. He achieved significant success last season, leading Denver to the AFC Championship game before going down with a foot injury. He looks to pick up where he left off, having serious aspirations of getting his squad to the Super Bowl. They got off to a slow start, but they have since put together a solid stretch of wins to assert themselves in the playoff race. Beating the Chiefs added a valuable win to their resume, showing off their status as serious playoff contenders. Nix reflected on the comeback after the game, thanking the fans for staying and giving the team all their support. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Something’s magical about this place. I don’t know. I can’t explain it,” Nix said on the CBS broadcast. "Something's magical about this place. I don't know. I can't explain it." Bo Nix speaks to @tracywolfson after a WILD @Broncos comeback pic.twitter.com/WsGCdSQNQP — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) November 2, 2026 How Bo Nix, Broncos played against Chiefs Bo Nix and the Broncos dug deep to pull off the comeback against Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs. Denver fans are certainly thankful for it, getting to see their team take down one of the best squads in the NFL. Kansas City boasted the upper hand for most of the matchup, taking 24-13 lead going into the fourth quarter. Denver came alive in the last 15 minutes of regulation, scoring the last 15 points of the memorable contest. Nix enjoyed a solid performance leading the balanced offense. He completed 20 out of 32 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns. Jonah Coleman was active as a rusher and pass-catcher for Denver. He racked up 11 carries for 41 yards and a touchdown while catching four passes for 63 yards. Courtland Sutton came next with four catches for 53 yards, Jaylen Waddle had three receptions for 39 yards and a touchdown, while Nate Adkins caught two passes for four yards and a touchdown. The Broncos will look forward to their next matchup, being on the road. They take on the Carolina Panthers in Week 9 as kickoff commences on Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET. item.title: Mike Tomlin hits Cowboys with brutally honest reality check after Cardinals game
item.description: Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Mike Tomlin hits Cowboys with brutally honest reality check after Cardinals game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coach Brian Schottenheimer ’s Dallas Cowboys fell to 3-5 with a 33-30 overtime, home loss to the caused the Cowboys coach to speak about personal responsibility . Quarterback Dak Prescott attempted to shield his head coach from criticism afterward, but Mike Tomlin entered the fray with criticisms of his own as he spoke on Sunday Night Football later on in the night. Ari Meirov shared Tomlin’s comments, which were not sugarcoated as he tore into the Cowboys. “I saw a bunch of blinkers, and what I mean by that, if you’re a blinker, cut your eyelids off. What I mean is, you gotta relish the thick moments, you gotta want to make the play, as an individual or particular units that wanted to grab the bull by the horns and win the game. Certainly their defense, we can spend a lot of time talking about that two-minute drive and things of that nature, but their offense had a short field when they had an unsuccessful onside kick at the end of regulation, and then they went three-and-out in overtime, and so I see a team that doesn’t have anybody that wants to be the unit to secure victory, they gotta cut their eyelids off.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Cowboys lost tight end Jake Ferguson early in the game which led to a sub-200 yard passing day from QB Dak Prescott. Javonte Williams led the running game with 56 yards but it wasn’t enough to inspire much hope, on a day that saw a NSFW explosion by Cowboys owner Jerry Jones . Tomlin’s words were harsh in nature, but seemed fitting given the Cowboys’ latest collapse. At 3-5, they have a chance to make a run in a mediocre NFC East division, but likely won’t be anyone’s choice to make noise in the playoffs, if they make it that far. Related: Cowboys’ miserable meltdown vs. Cardinals breaks incredible 69-game streak Related: Brian Schottenheimer knows Cowboys let him down vs. Cardinals, but he won’t tell you when

item.title: Cowboys’ miserable meltdown vs. Cardinals breaks incredible 69-game streak
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Cowboys’ miserable meltdown vs. Cardinals breaks incredible 69-game streak appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . You could get hit by a giant asteroid or eaten by a killer whale, and you still would not feel as terrible as the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday. The Cowboys blew a 14-point lead in the fourth quarter and lost to the Arizona Cardinals, 33-30, in overtime, much to the sheer despair of the home crowd at AT&T Stadium. Chad Ryland kicked the game-winning field goal from 42 yards, redeeming himself after failing to convert the extra point that would have finished off the Cowboys in regulation. Arizona and Dallas each have a 3-5 record. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) According to ESPN’s Todd Archer, the Cowboys snapped a decades-long streak after their monumental collapse. “Before Sunday, the Cowboys were 69-0 since 2000 when leading by 14 points or more in the fourth quarter. They are now 69-1,” wrote Archer on X. Dak Prescott went 19-of-29 for 195 yards and one touchdown. He was sacked four times. He scored on a rush at the 14:20 mark of the fourth quarter to increase Dallas’ lead to 24-10. Then it was all downhill from there. In a report from the Associated Press’ Schuyler Dixon, Prescott admitted that it was “very disappointing.” “One of the toughest (losses), I guess, I’ve been a part of. No other words for it really, other than really, really disappointing, frustrating. It’s part of this league,” said the veteran quarterback. The Cowboys allowed 467 yards, including 80 yards in eight plays in the closing minute of regulation. Despite the painful loss and the mediocre campaign, owner Jerry Jones said he is not keen on firing anybody . The Cowboys will battle the Indianapolis Colts in Week 9. Related: Mike Tomlin hits Cowboys with brutally honest reality check after Cardinals game Related: Brian Schottenheimer knows Cowboys let him down vs. Cardinals, but he won’t tell you when

item.title: Dak Prescott’s blunt admission puts Brian Schottenheimer under pressure after Cowboys loss
item.description: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images Dak Prescott has admitted the Dallas Cowboys needed to be more aggressive during their overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals, adding to the pressure on head coach Brian Schottenheimer after another disappointing offensive performance. Dallas managed just 261 total yards in the defeat while its defence gave up 467. The result leaves the Cowboys at 3-5 and raises further questions about their ability to turn the season around. Prescott completed 19 of 29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown. He also rushed for 20 yards and another score, but his comments after the game drew attention to the Cowboys’ offensive approach. Dak Prescott wants Brian Schottenheimer to be more aggressive with Dallas Cowboys Speaking to reporters after the loss, Prescott defended Schottenheimer but admitted he would have preferred a different approach against Arizona. “Yeah, I wish we would’ve been more aggressive there.” The quarterback did not directly criticise his head coach, but his admission comes at a difficult time for Schottenheimer. Dallas has struggled offensively in three of its last four games, leaving the coaching staff under increasing scrutiny. Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones was also questioned about Schottenheimer’s position following the defeat. However, Jones insisted the problems extended beyond the head coach. “That’s not in my mind at this time,” Jones said. “This is an indictment of the whole show … This is a criticism of everyone.” Jones also acknowledged that he had previously made a mid-season coaching change, referring to Wade Phillips, but dismissed the possibility of doing the same with Schottenheimer. “I’m not proud of it, but I made a change with Wade Phillips there in the middle of the season,” Jones added. “I don’t see that here at all.” Despite that reassurance, Jones made it clear that the Cowboys’ performances were unacceptable and that responsibility rested with everyone involved. “Well, I don’t know,” Jones said when asked whether he was worried about Schottenheimer. “None of us are getting it done and that should be my concern.” The Cowboys now need to find answers quickly, particularly on offence. Prescott remains central to their hopes of recovering from their poor start, but Schottenheimer’s play-calling will face further scrutiny if Dallas cannot produce a more convincing performance in its next game. item.title: Part 4: 2026-27 SoCon Preview: The lower tier and the longshots
item.description: SPARTANBURG, SC - FEBRUARY 10: The Citadel Bulldogs guard Keynan Davis (22) during a college basketball game between The Citadel Bulldogs and the Wofford Terriers on February 10, 2024 at Jerry Richardson Indoor Stadium in Spartanburg, S.C. (Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The final portion of the 2026-27 Mid-Major Madness preview series for SoCon basketball takes a look at three unique situations, with newcomer Tennessee Tech introducing an new unknown into the equation, and with a loaded roster, the Golden Eagles will without question compete right away, but can they handle the rigors of a road environment on a random Wednesday night in the SoCon at Cameron Hall or Timmons Arena? What about the home atmosphere? Can the Hooper-Eblen Center keep on par with a majority of the league’s other home venues and become an intimidating fortress? Then, there is The Citadel, which brings perhaps more momentum into a season than it has in over a decade since the last time Ed Conroy was the head coach. The Bulldogs have put together their most talented portal class to date under Conroy, and if preseason results are any indicator of projected success, than being a “long shot” in this tough league might be much too low of expectation for The Citadel in 2026-27. Still, as talented as the Bulldogs are, they have to go out and prove that they are the real deal and not the Bulldogs we’ve known so many times before. Finally, UNCG brings a new coach on-board, in Jerod Haase, and the big question is can this program recover its status as being a perennial title contender, and if so, how long will it take Haase to build that strong foundation and rebuild that winning culture that the Spartans were able to build and sustain under Wes Miller and Mike Jones for the past 11 seasons, winning 233 games, which is the second most wins only to Furman’s 245 victories in that same span. Tennessee Tech (13-19, 8-12 OVC/ninth) Change is something that has been needed for a long time in Cookeville for the men’s basketball program at Tennessee Tech. The dominoes started to fall in favor of change even before the 2025-26 season when it was announced in July 2025 that the Golden Eagles would be joining the SoCon as its newest league member. Then came the 2025-26 season for the Golden Eagles, which would turn out to be a very disappointing one in their final season in the OVC. It was out with a whimper, as the Golden Eagles failed to qualify for even the OVC Tournament, as Tech finished one place out of being eligible for the conference tournament. That led to the dismissal of former head coach John Pelphrey and the naming of Tobin Anderson as the head coach in the spring. TTU also renovated its locker rooms at the Hooper-Eblen Center. item.title: Blue Jays Catcher Snubbed Of Historic Award
item.description: Blue Jays make Brandon Valenzuela decision. Getty PHOENIX, ARIZONA - APRIL 19: Brandon Valenzuela #59 of the Toronto Blue Jaysduring the MLB game at Chase Field on April 19, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona. The Blue Jays defeated the Diamondbacks 10-4. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) Getty Thanks to his strong defensive season in what was his first full campaign as a member of the Toronto Blue Jays, catcher Brandon Valenzuela was named a finalist for the American League Gold Glove Award. However, he’ll have to wait for a different season to take home the award, as it was ultimately claimed by Detroit Tigers catcher Dillon Dingler for a second straight campaign. Toronto Blue Jays Catcher Brandon Valenzuela Was Snubbed For The Gold Glove Award Getty PHOENIX, ARIZONA – APRIL 19: Brandon Valenzuela #59 of the Toronto Blue Jays during the MLB game at Chase Field on April 19, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona. The Blue Jays defeated the Diamondbacks 10-4. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) This season’s recipient of the American League Gold Glove award was Detroit Tigers catcher Dillon Dingler, who took home the award for the second straight season. Unfortunately, this means that Valenzuela will have to wait for a different season to take home the award, which would have been the first of his career. However, the good news is that Blue Jays fans can take comfort in his emergence as one of the top defensive players in the American League, and if his upward career trajectory continues, it might not be long before he hears his name called for the award in the future. Valenzuela Is Coming Off His First Full Year With The Blue Jays Valenzuela began his professional career with the Padres after signing in 2017. He eventually emerged as a standout in the minors, earning Texas League Player of the Month honors in June 2024 with San Antonio. Toronto acquired him from San Diego at the 2025 trade deadline in the deal that sent Will Wagner to the Padres. Valenzuela spent the rest of the season with Triple-A Buffalo before being protected on the Blue Jays’ 40-man roster. He started 2026 in Buffalo but quickly reached the majors when Toronto needed catching depth following Alejandro Kirk’s injury. Valenzuela debuted in early April and recorded his first MLB homer five days later against the Twins . He would finish the 2026 campaign hitting .226 with nine home runs and 24 RBI, along with a .688 OPS. item.title: I confronted religious merchants in Kaduna to achieve peace — Uba Sani
item.description: By Charles Kumolu For years, Kaduna State was synonymous with ethno-religious violence, communal distrust, and bloodshed, with successive administrations struggling to end the cycle of killings that fractured communities and undermined the state’s economic and social life. But Governor Uba Sani believes the tide has turned, insisting that the peace being experienced in the state is the product of deliberate efforts to dismantle what he calls the “merchants of ethno-religious crises,” promote inclusive governance, and address the economic conditions that fuel insecurity. From Southern Kaduna to Birnin Gwari, he says, the emphasis has been on rebuilding trust, taking development to neglected communities, and making citizens see one another as partners rather than adversaries. In this interview with a team of editors from Vanguard Newspapers, the governor explains the thinking behind his Kaduna Model, how his administration secured the release of 222 captives in Birnin Gwari through the reopening of markets, and why he believes economic empowerment is central to sustainable peace. He also responds to allegations of intolerance toward opposition politicians, speaks on the role of political elites in exploiting ethnic and religious divisions, and outlines his administration’s efforts to reposition Kaduna through agriculture, rural roads, transportation, and sports infrastructure. In Rivers State’s history, it was once known as Rivers of Blood. About 10 years ago, Kaduna was known as a state of blood, crisis, and bloodshed. How were you able to restore peace, especially in Southern Kaduna? When we came in, the first thing we looked at was recognising the fact that our state is the most diverse state in Nigeria. Of course, I agree with you that the number of lives we lost in Kaduna in the last 20 years, before we came, was more than the number of lives lost because of insurgency, kidnapping, and banditry. Knowing that, we believed that for us to claim any success as a government, we must bring our people together. The only way we could do that was by ensuring that we created a state where everyone would be carried along in whatever we were doing. Of course, we decided to run a system that would bring everyone together, which is a highly inclusive government. For us, inclusivity isn’t just about bringing people to sit with us. It’s about taking development to every part of Kaduna State. When we came in, we looked at the deficits in terms of infrastructure, healthcare, and education. We looked at this holistically, and we believed it was the only way we could address injustice and marginalisation. Some people felt they were not treated like citizens of our state. We believed that doing that really demanded that we relegate politics and elevate governance. Doing that, of course, could sometimes be difficult because when you are elected as a governor, you have people who work with you. item.title: Patrick Mahomes Sends Veiled Message to NFL on Chiefs-Broncos Controversy
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 25: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs looks on against the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter at Lumen Field on October 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty The Kansas City Chiefs are officially on a losing streak, but for a brief moment it appeared Patrick Mahomes led another magical game-winning drive against the Denver Broncos. Instead, the touchdown was negated as the referees called a false start. When asked about the controversial call, Mahomes initially attempted to take the high road by backing the call before adding that in game-deciding moments “the little stuff doesn’t get called like that.” “I have not seen it, but like it didn’t surprise me or catch me or anything like that, so it couldn’t have been big, but it was called,” Mahomes told reporters on November 1, following the Chiefs’ loss to the Broncos. “I mean, at the end of the day, you have to go with whatever is called, but a lot of times in those big moments the little stuff doesn’t get called like that.” Chiefs HC Andy Reid Disagreed With Late Penalty Call vs. Broncos It is worth noting that Kansas City had another opportunity to score even after the five-yard penalty, but Mahomes was sacked on the final play of the game. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid was a bit more direct about the controversial call. “I didn’t see it,” Reid said of the late penalty that negated a potential touchdown, per ESPN’s Nate Taylor. “I saw him move his head, but I didn’t see [a false start].” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Patrick Mahomes Sends Veiled Message to NFL on Chiefs-Broncos Controversy appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Victor Wembanyama speaks on how his blood clot problem in 2025 changed his life
item.description: Victor Wembanyama speaks on how his blood clot problem in 2025 changed his life originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Victor Wembanyama has proven that he is one of the league's best players over the past three years. However, he has already dealt with some serious health problems, but they were not the lower-body injuries that people thought he would get in the NBA. The biggest health scare that Wembanyama has faced was the blood clots he dealt with in early 2025. It was such a big part of Wemby's life that he made sure to learn a lot of lessons from that scary experience that prematurely ended his 2024-25 campaign with the San Antonio Spurs . Victor Wembanyama reveals the lessons he learned from his blood clot issues Wembanyama has always dealt with problems head-on, which is why he is such a good player. However, the deep vein thrombosis or blood clots were a problem that he struggled against, especially since, if it was worse, it was life-threatening. Thankfully, Wembanyama listened to the medical professionals, so that led to him having a much better life. It has also changed his outlook on his personal life and career. That is a big deal for Wembanyama because it felt like he grew up during that debacle with the blood clots. That helped him mature and be more expressive, which is why that was a big part of the Spurs ' run to the NBA Finals last season. MORE: Victor Wembanyama has revealed the biggest lesson he learned from Gregg Popovich Now, Wembanyama is a much more emotional person because he knows that he does not have to hide anything after going through what he went through. Wemby is much more vocal with his team, and his team understands that he is more expressive now. "The condition I had in early 2025, the thrombosis, had a huge impact on this. After that it’s like, life’s so short, I don’t even want to waste it being somebody else. Simple as that," Wembanyama said on 60 Minutes about how his blood clots changed how he looked at life . While it may seem like that is only affected his personal life, it has certainly affected his game as well. He is much more expressive with his game, and his emotions drive him to perform much better, as seen in the series against the Oklahoma City Thunder in the Western Conference Finals. As long as Wemby continues to improve his game and regulation his emotions better, he will continue to be a star player. He is ready to take the next step, and that is to the best human and athlete he can be moving forward. item.title: Patrick Mahomes Bracing For ‘Dogfight’ For AFC West After Broncos Loss
item.description: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 01: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs leaves the field after his team's 28-24 loss against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field At Mile High on November 01, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) Getty A late false start penalty on right tackle Jaylon Moore stripped the Kansas City Chiefs of a game-winning touchdown with just four seconds left on the clock in the game, down four points at home against division rivals, the Denver Broncos. A sack on the final play of the game sealed the Chiefs’ fate, and saw the Chiefs move to 5-2 on the season and surrender top position in the AFC West. Having not won the division for the first in a decade last season, KC will no doubt be more cognizant than ever to not take divisional games for granted. Especially now that they lie second to Denver. Mahomes Ready to Battle it Out For AFC West After Defeat Speaking to the media after the game, Mahomes spoke about the state of the division half-way through the season, claiming that both them and the Broncos were in a “dogfight” for the division. Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes: "Now, you're kind of in a dogfight for the division… You have to take it one week at a time." He says he's proud of how the guys battled, but they have to find a way to get back in the win column after two straight losses. — Charles Goldman (@goldmctNFL) November 2, 2026 “Now, you’re kind of in a dogfight for the division… You have to take it one week at a time.” Mahomes said after the game, per Charles Goldman. “Last week we didn’t have the fight that we had this week. I thought the fight was better this week. Whenever you’re playing up against a really good football team. But at the end a loss is a loss and you learn from it, you move on from it and we’re still early in the season.” Mahomes continued . Chiefs Looking to Bounce Back After Second Defeat This loss marks the Chiefs’ fourth to the Broncos out of the last five, the sole win being the opening week of the season back in mid-September. And coming now off consecutive losses to Seattle and Denver, the emphasis will be on getting back to basics and back on track. Entering a slightly easier run of games than two of final four teams from last year’s playoffs, in the Jets, Falcons and Cardinals , Kansas City will be hoping that 5-2 soon becomes 8-2 before they embark on a brutal five-game stretch that sees them take on the Bills, Rams, Bengals, Patriots and 49ers. item.title: Predators Buy Low on Shane Wright in Trade with Kraken
item.description: The Nashville Predators bought low on Shane Wright, hoping that this deal would be one of those that pay off big time. Getty The Nashville Predators pulled off a bit of a surprising trade on Sunday, landing former fourth-overall pick Shane Wright from the Seattle Kraken. The deal was a classic example of buying low. After months of speculation, the Kraken cut bait on Wright, a player the organization swore it would not sell low. The deal wasn’t that bad, as the Kraken got back another former first-rounder, Matthew Wood. 🔄 TRADE We've received forward Shane Wright from Seattle in exchange for forward Matthew Wood. Full details » https://t.co/AbgYZiQ0Va pic.twitter.com/SWDPCTpDNA — Nashville Predators (@PredsNHL) November 1, 2026 The Predators are trying to make the most of an opportunity. It was plainly evident that Wright never really got on in Seattle. He had two tough seasons in which the Kraken avoided burning the first year of his entry-level deal. When the organization finally decided to give him a real shot, it seemed he had arrived. During the 2024-25 season, Wright scored 19 goals and 44 points. Those totals, however, seem like a mirage. He slumped the following year, leading to questions about his consistency. This season, it seemed the Kraken had enough. The 22-year-old has three goals and four points in 14 games. While his offensive numbers haven’t been atrocious, Shane Wright’s overall game hasn’t been commensurate with his draft status. And it’s that situation that prompted the team to seek a trade. The Kraken were hoping that some other organization would put together a decent offer that would land them a top-six scorer. Alas, that wasn’t exactly what the Predators did. What Does Nashville Gain From Shane Wright Trade So, what do the Predators gain from this Shane Wright trade? On the surface, the Preds are taking on a reclamation project. GM Chris MacFarland is trying to bank on Wright’s upside. He’s still 22 and has plenty of runway to show that he can become a legit top-six forward in the NHL. That situation may actually pan out by playing alongside consummate pros like Steven Stamkos and Ryan O’Reilly. And O’Reilly may very well be the reason why the Predators made this move. The veteran center will be a UFA at the end of the season, and, well, it’s uncertain whether O’Reilly will return to Nashville next season. Now, it’s far too soon to anoint Shane Wright as O’Reilly’s successor. But at least his acquisition gives the Predators something to work with. Predators Gain a Flippable Asset Ultimately, the NHL is a business. MacFarland understands that well. And if things work out well for Shane Wright in Nashville, the club could have a flippable asset at the deadline. The Preds are teetering between a rebuild and contending. Thus far, Nashville has been one of those in-betweeners. But as the season wears on, it will become evident where they stand. And if the Predators decide to sell, a successful and productive Shane Wright might

item.title: OPEC+ holds December oil output steady to support market stability
item.description: By Udeme Akpan, Energy Editor The Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and its allies, known as OPEC+, have agreed to maintain their September 2026 required production levels for December to support stability in the global oil market. The countries — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman — reached the agreement at a virtual meeting on November 1, 2026, where they reviewed “global market conditions and outlook”. The seven producers, which announced additional voluntary production adjustments in April and November 2023, decided to retain their existing production requirements for December. In a statement after the meeting, the countries reaffirmed their commitment to cooperation among oil-producing nations and stability in the international market. The statement read: “The seven participating countries decided to maintain September 2026 required production for December 2026.” The countries also reiterated their “collective commitment to achieve full conformity with the Declaration of Cooperation”, the framework guiding collaboration between OPEC members and participating non-OPEC oil producers. They added that they would continue to monitor developments in the global oil market through regular consultations. “The seven OPEC+ countries will continue to hold monthly meetings to review market conditions. The next meeting will be held on 29 November 2026,” the statement said. The seven countries’ combined required production level for December stands at 31.01 million barrels per day (bpd), according to the accompanying production schedule. Saudi Arabia has the highest required production level at 10.478 million bpd, followed by Russia with 9.949 million bpd and Iraq with 4.431 million bpd. Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman have required production levels of 2.676 million bpd, 1.628 million bpd, 1.007 million bpd and 841,000 bpd, respectively. Reacting to the development in an interview, an energy analyst, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the decision could support international crude oil prices, with positive implications for Nigeria’s revenue and foreign exchange earnings. item.title: Diri has betrayed Bayelsa to APC, says Dickson; ‘We won’t respond’ — Gov’s aide
item.description: By Samuel Oyadongha Yenagoa—Former Bayelsa State Governor, Seriake Dickson, has accused his successor, Governor Douye Diri, of surrendering government they built together to a party that never won the state through the ballot. Dickson, who spoke in a statement following his homecoming to Bayelsa, weekend, which witnessed the commissioning of the NDC state secretariat, said the governor’s decision to join the APC amounted to ‘donating’ the state to a party he claimed had never won Bayelsa through the ballot. The National Leader of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) said he had deliberately refrained from commenting extensively on developments in the state to avoid creating political tension and preserve peace. He, however, declared that the time had come to make his political position clear, accusing Diri of abandoning the political structure that nurtured and supported his emergence as governor. He said: “Every single one of the people in the current government was nurtured and supported for years by me.” The former governor recalled that Diri served as his Executive Secretary, Deputy Chief of Staff, member of the House of Representatives and Senator before succeeding him as governor. Dickson said his decision to support Diri’s emergence was informed by the need to sustain Ijaw political leadership and promote fairness among the different local government areas in Bayelsa. He alleged that his successor had now turned against those who supported his political journey, accusing the administration of pettiness, propaganda, blackmail and victimisation. “Our victory was donated free of charge to the APC, making all of us overnight opposition members in our own state, in a government we formed, in a governorship I crafted, and an administration we worked hard to put in power,” he said. Dickson maintained that the APC had never defeated him or won Bayelsa State at the polls, claiming that his political influence had prevented the party from taking control of the state since 2015. He expressed disappointment that Diri had aligned with the APC without securing what he described as corresponding benefits for Bayelsa from the Federal Government. The senator also criticised the Federal Government over what he described as inadequate infrastructure development and insufficient representation of Bayelsa and the Niger Delta in federal appointments. He, however, urged his supporters to remain peaceful and avoid personal attacks against the governor. “As I said, children may deny their father, but fathers do not deny children. The governor is still my person, my brother, my compatriot and our governor. But he is now someone I disagree with, as he and the people in his government are wrong with the direction they are taking our state to,” he said. Diri won’t respond — Aide An aide to Governor Diri, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the governor would not respond to Dickson’s allegations. “The governor doesn’t want to respond to him. item.title: 3 feared dead, 5 rescued as two-storey building collapses in Osun
item.description: By Shina Abubakar OSOGBO—THREE persons have been confirmed dead and five rescued alive after a two-storey commercial building under construction collapsed at Owode-Ede, in Ede North Local Government Area of Osun State. The incident occurred at Zone 8, Oke Alaafia Community, at about 11pm on Friday, prompting a rescue operation by the Federal Fire Service and other emergency responders. In a statement, the spokesperson for the Federal Fire Service, Osun State Command, DSF Ojo Omoyemi Olamide, said the command received a distress call through its emergency line at about 11:30pm and immediately mobilised personnel to the scene. She said the five rescued victims were taken to Idera Specialist Hospital, Ede, for urgent medical attention, while the three bodies recovered were handed over to the Nigeria Police Force, A Division, Ede. “The incident involved a two-storey shopping complex used for commercial purposes. The building consists of six shops on the upper floor, six shops on the middle floor and two stores on the ground floor, covering an area of about 50m by 100m. “Preliminary investigation reveals that structural defects and the use of substandard materials are suspected to be the cause of the collapse,” she stated. Olamide said the rescue operation was completed and personnel returned to the station at about 9:26am on Saturday. She added that the estimated property loss was N100 million, while property worth approximately N150 million was saved. The operation was conducted in collaboration with the Osun State Fire Service, Ede Station; the Nigeria Police Force, A Division, Ede; and personnel of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Owode-Ede Division. item.title: Gunmen abduct Plateau varsity student, shoot another in Bokkos
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS—GUNMEN suspected to be kidnappers have abducted a 100-level female student of Plateau State University (PLASU), Bokkos, and shot another person during an attack on an off-campus student residential area in Bokkos Local Government Area of Plateau State. The incidents occurred on Saturday at about 8:40pm, raising concerns over the safety of students living outside the university campus. A student, who spoke on condition of anonymity, confirmed the abduction to journalists in Jos on Sunday, saying the victim had gone out with another female student when she was seized. “Yes, the student was taken away by the attackers last night, and we have not seen her since then. She lives off-campus, but I don’t know her personally,” the student said. He lamented the growing insecurity in the area and appealed to security agencies to ensure the safe rescue of the abducted student. A university staff member, who also spoke on condition of anonymity because he was not authorised to comment publicly, said the institution was aware of the incident. “The university is aware of a reported shooting incident in one of the off-campus student residential areas. This would be the second such incident in four weeks,” he said. “While the incident did not occur within the university campus, which remains our direct responsibility to secure, we are deeply concerned that any of our students living off-campus should face such threats to their safety,” he added. The staff member said the administration of Prof. Shadrack Best had made concerted efforts to provide safe on-campus accommodation for all students. “However, due to severe financial constraints, the university is currently only able to accommodate about 1,000 students in its dormitories,” he stated. “The university appreciates the support of its Visitor and Plateau State Governor, Barr. Caleb Manasseh Mutfwang, as well as the Tertiary Education Trust Fund, TETFund, for providing critical infrastructure at the institution,” he said. “The university will continue to engage relevant authorities to expand both accommodation and security for our nearly 20,000 students,” he added. Efforts to reach the Plateau State Police Command’s Public Relations Officer, SP Alfred Alabo, for comments were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. The post Gunmen abduct Plateau varsity student, shoot another in Bokkos appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: APOD: 2026 November 2 – A Long Cloud on Mars
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 2 – A… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. A Long Cloud on Mars Explanation: What’s causing this unusually long cloud on Mars ? Known as the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud (AMEC) and first recorded by NASA’s Viking Orbiter 2 in 1977, the strange cloud has been imaged in greater detail more recently by ESA ’s robotic Mars Express spacecraft. The featured image is from 2018. The cloud forms only during spring and summer seasons and then only during morning hours. Made of water-ice, the most familiar process that causes cloud crystals to form around bits of dust would fail due to the thinness and lack of dust high in the Martian atmosphere . Leading speculation holds that dust is not involved. After the cloud forms near the volcano Arsia Mons , wind blows the cloud downstream — creating a tail that can extend over 1500 kilometers. Efforts to better understand AMEC s will continue, an understanding that may bolster a more complete view of cloud formation on Earth . item.title: Monarch’s murder: Nwifuru seeks death penalty for kidnappers
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo Ebonyi State Government has forwarded an executive bill to the State House of Assembly seeking to make kidnapping a capital offence punishable by death without an option of alternative punishment. Governor Francis Nwifuru disclosed this at the weekend during the funeral of the slain traditional ruler of Ndufu-Alike autonomous community in Ikwo Local Government Area, HRH Eze Francis Igwe. Igwe, father of the immediate past Deputy Governor of Ebonyi State, Eric Igwe, was abducted on Sunday, March 1, while on his way to church. He was reportedly killed by his abductors a day after. Speaking at the funeral, conducted by the Assemblies of God Church, Nwifuru lamented what he described as the moral deterioration among Nigerian youths, expressing concern about their readiness to assume leadership positions in the future. He also pledged to implement any court decision against those arrested over the monarch’s murder, adding that the proposed legislation was intended to deter kidnapping and abduction in the state. The governor said: “I am worried about our present-day youths taking up leadership positions tomorrow. Some of our youths are not well informed, and they act so irrationally. “I am concerned because, with some of their attitudinal dispositions, there seems to be no future for our youths. “The youths need to have a rethink concerning certain actions of theirs, especially as concerns their attitudes towards community leaders. They should desist from treating their leaders as holders of their destinies.” He warned that the monarch’s murder should be the last such incident in Ikwo and other parts of the state. “I will not wait to execute the decision of the court over the murderers of this monarch, HRH Eze Francis Igwe. We have sent a bill to the House of Assembly to make kidnapping attract the death sentence by hanging in the state, with no other option. This should serve as a deterrent to those planning a kidnap, whether for political reasons or otherwise,” the governor said. Nwifuru described the late monarch as a forthright, vocal and astute parliamentarian who represented his people effectively in the old Anambra State and attracted development projects to his community, including the popular Folk Technical College, which has produced prominent Nigerians. In tributes, former governors Sam Egwu and Martin Elechi, as well as former Senate President, Anyim Pius Anyim, described the deceased as a statesman, peacemaker, renowned educationist, administrator and passionate leader who left enduring legacies. They urged the family and the Ikwo people to take solace in his contributions to society. In his tribute, the monarch’s first son, Igwe, described his father as a devoted family man and role model who guided him on family life, religion, politics and culture. He said the circumstances surrounding his father’s death remained difficult for the family to comprehend but expressed confidence that his legacies would endure across generati

item.title: How melted nylon additive keeps plantain chips crunchy
item.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan For some years, plantain chip has been one of Nigeria’s ultimate snacks which is affordable, accessible, and portable. But as inflation hovers at historic highs, a sinister economic survival tactic has crept into the informal food sector. Read Also: NAFDAC secures five-year jail term for fake Goya oil manufacturer Economy&Lifestyle discovered that to cut costs and keep chips crispy for days, some street entrepreneurs are turning to a dangerous additive: melted cellophane bags. The cost of a crunch The mathematics of running a small-scale food business in Nigeria today is brutal. The price of vegetable oil, cooking gas, and raw plantains has tripled over the last two years. For vendors like Halima Mohammed, who operates a roadside frying station, the pressure to maintain profit margins without raising prices is suffocating. “If I increase the price of a small pack from N200 to N400, the students will walk away. “People don’t have money. So, vendors look for shortcuts to make the oil last longer and keep the chips from getting soggy in humidity.” The “shortcut” involves tossing polyethylene plastic bags directly into the scalding oil. As the plastic melts, it blends with the vegetable oil, creating a glazing agent. When the plantain slices are fried in this mixture, they form a glassy, ultra-crisp outer shell. Crucially for vendors, the plastic coating prevents the chips from absorbing moisture, extending their shelf life from two days to over two weeks. A lifestyle of hustle and denial In the underbelly of Nigeria’s entrepreneurial ecosystem, the practice is an open secret, driven by sheer desperation. The lifestyle of a micro-entrepreneur in Nigeria is defined by any-way-raw-iron—a slang term for survival by any means necessary. With no safety nets and a failing grid that forces reliance on expensive petrol generators, the boundary between ethical business and hazardous malpractice has blurred. Osaro Jimoh, a distributor who supplies packaged chips to traffic vendors on the , admitted that the market rewards the longest-lasting product. “The boys selling in traffic need chips that stay crunchy under the hot sun for days. If the chips go soft, the motorists will throw them back at us. Nobody asks how the crunch is made; they just want the crunch. “I don’t know the preservative used to achieve such crunchiness.” For the millions of consumers who rely on these cheap snacks to get through grueling multi-hour commutes, the lifestyle implications are passive but deadly. Plastic-infused oil releases carcinogenic compounds, heavy metals, and microplastics into the food, posing severe long-term risks to liver and kidney health. The regulatory blindspot Agencies have repeatedly warned the public against consuming street foods prepared with plastic additives. However, enforcing regulations in a vast, informal economy is nearly impossible. Millions of fryers operate out of residential backyards, unbranded and untraceable. Public health

item.title: Pennsylvania’s Grand Canyon
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Pennsylvania’s Grand Canyon Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search October 25, 2026 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison North-central Pennsylvania is canyon country with an Appalachian flair. Pine Creek Gorge reaches depths of about 1,500 feet (460 meters) along its gently curving path through the forests of the Allegheny Plateau . Instead of the steep rock walls characteristic of canyons in the desert Southwest, lushly vegetated slopes outline the dramatic topography. In autumn, greens give way to a palette of reds and golds sought out by leaf peepers. Nicknamed the “Grand Canyon of Pennsylvania,” the gorge runs for some 45 miles (72 kilometers) from Ansonia south to Pine Creek’s confluence with the West Branch Susquehanna River, reaching its greatest depths around Waterville. The OLI (Operational Land Imager) on the NASA-USGS Landsat 8 satellite captured this image of Pine Creek Gorge on October 25, 2026, when colorful fall foliage was on display. Glaciers played a key role in the canyon’s formation, though ice itself did not carve it. Pine Creek once flowed to the north , opposite of what it does today. As glaciers advanced into the region from the northeast during the last ice age, they dammed the river and filled the valley with lakes. Those lakes eventually overflowed, sending water streaming to the south. Autumn colors emerge along Pine Creek Gorge in this view from Colton Point State Park on October 11, 2009. fishhawk , via Flickr When the ice receded, Pine Creek was already becoming entrenched in its southward course. Rocks and sand left behind by the melting ice further prevented the water from turning back north. Glacial meltwater continued to rush through the valley, deepening and shaping it into its current form. Today, the hillsides around the gorge are blanketed in northern hardwood and mixed oak forest, sprinkled with hemlock and white pine. In autumn, the deciduous trees impart red and gold hues to the landscape akin to the rock of the famous Arizona canyon . item.title: Gully erosion destroys 30 houses, cuts off Edo communities
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY — No fewer than 30 houses have been destroyed by a ravaging gully erosion at Agor-Uwagboe community in Oredo Local Government Area of Edo State. The erosion has also cut off the community’s access road linking it with Ofumwengbe and Egbiri communities, leaving residents with limited means of movement. To ease the situation, residents have constructed a makeshift wooden bridge to enable motorcycles conveying passengers to cross the affected area. Residents of the community on Sunday staged a peaceful protest to draw the attention of the Edo State Government to their worsening situation. Speaking during the protest, a community member, Mr Ernest Uwagboe, said the gully was gradually extending into the community, threatening more homes and property. He warned that the entire community could be consumed by the erosion within three years if the state government failed to urgently intervene. The community’s spokesman, Kenneth Adoni, said residents had written several letters to relevant government agencies seeking assistance but had yet to receive any intervention. He appealed to Governor Monday Okpebholo to come to their aid, lamenting the hardship caused by the erosion. “We are begging Governor Monday Okpebholo to come and help us. For the past three years, the gully has caused lots of problems. We cannot cross to other communities. Whenever it rains, children cannot go to school,” he said. The residents called on the state government to urgently address the erosion menace and restore access to neighbouring communities to prevent further destruction and alleviate their hardship. item.title: Britain shouldn’t apologise for slave trade; Africa profited — Kemi Badenoch
item.description: By Nkiruka Nnorom, with agency report Leader of UK’s Conservative Party, Kemi Badenoch, has urged British not to apologise for its role in transatlantic slave trade, saying it would amount to a “navel-gazing distraction”, and would be used as lever for financial compensation by campaigners. Her comments came as UK’s PM, Andy Burnham, said he was considering a formal apology, before he flies to the Commonwealth heads of government meeting (CHOGM) in Antigua and Barbuda next week. Speaking to broadcasters yesterday, Badenoch described slavery as an evil “in which people from every continent and region participated”. She also questioned whether it was worth future leaders attending the Commonwealth summit, given that it was now dominated by calls for reparations. In an article for the Guardian, Burnham said there would not be reparations in the form of financial compensation, but said he was prepared to engage in helping poorer countries restructure debt on more favourable terms. But reacting, Badenoch said leaders should be “honest about the whole history, not select the parts that are politically convenient today, especially given Britain’s leading role in ending the transatlantic slave trade”. She wrote in a social media post: “If Caribbean countries are asking Britain for a formal apology for Britain’s role in the transatlantic slave trade, will they also be asking the same of the descendants of African kingdoms, rulers and merchants who captured, sold and profited from the trade?” “On demands for reparations, whether through cash or debt relief, we have been down this track before,” she said. Badenoch recalled that campaigns such as Jubilee 2000, Drop the Debt and Make Poverty History had pushed for debt cancellation for poorer countries 25 years ago, leading to more than $100 billion in debt being written off. However, she noted that many of those countries had since accumulated even larger debts. Badenoch said Burnham’s apology was unnecessary because of comments made by Tony Blair two decades ago. “The Commonwealth should be looking forward, not endlessly backwards,” she posted. Badenoch told Sky News she believed that even if an apology was offered, campaigners would see it as a step towards financial compensation. “What I’m worried about is that this CHOGM summit is yet another opportunity for people to start asking Britain for money because of the slave trade. We need to start looking at how we can bring the Commonwealth together – start looking forwards, not backwards. “I don’t think we should be giving any money to compensate people for the slave trade, and I don’t think Andy Burnham needs to be apologising because it is a lever to wedge open the door to ask for cash.” Speaking in the same vein, UK’s Chancellor, John Healey, said it would be unfair for the British people to be hit financially for reparations when they had no role in the slave trade. “The prime minister has said, look, we are open to a discussion about an apology. He fee

item.title: Christians in Nigeria still face unspeakable violence — US Rep Moore
item.description: •Says fight against persecution must continue one year after CPC designation By Nkiruka Nnorom A member of United States House of Representatives, Riley Moore, has said Christians in Nigeria have continued to face unspeakable violence, one year after Nigeria was designated Country of Particular Concern, CPC. Moore stated this in a post on X to mark anniversary of designation of Nigeria as CPC by President Donald Trump. “Christians in Nigeria, and around the world, continue to face unspeakable violence. On this anniversary, we must rededicate our efforts to defend Christians in Nigeria and anywhere they face persecution,” Moore wrote. The lawmaker’s comment came as he reviewed impact of CPC designation, which he said was right decision by President Trump, alongside efforts by House Appropriations Republicans to condition aid to Nigeria and impose requirements to defend Christians, and advocacy by faith-based organisations. Moore said: “The President’s steadfast and decisive leadership, @houseappropsgop’s work to condition aid to Nigeria and impose requirements to defend Christians, and the tireless work of advocacy and faith based organizations has started to make a difference. “We saw the first Christmas without a massacre of Christians in recent memory. There is much more work to be done, but the government of Nigeria has shown signs of a willingness to address the violence against our brothers and sisters in Christ.” He had earlier noted that Nigeria witnessed first Christmas without massacre of Christians in recent memory, but said much more work needed to be done. Moore, however, hailed the federal government’s efforts, saying Abuja had shown signs of willingness to address violence. Nigeria was first designated as a Country of Particular Concern, CPC, by the United States in 2020 under President Donald Trump over alleged violations of religious freedom. The designation was delisted in 2021 by the Biden administration, a move that was criticised by some US lawmakers and faith-based groups. On November 2025, President Trump, on return to White House, redesignated Nigeria as CPC, citing continued attacks on Christian communities in Middle Belt and North-East. The CPC status under US International Religious Freedom Act allows Washington to impose policy options, including sanctions, aid restrictions and diplomatic pressure on countries adjudged to have engaged in or tolerated systematic violations of religious freedom. Following redesignation, House Appropriations Republicans moved to condition US assistance to Nigeria on demonstrable steps to protect Christians and prosecute perpetrators of religious-based violence. The federal government has consistently rejected characterisation of insecurity as religious persecution, arguing that terrorism by Boko Haram, ISWAP, banditry and farmer-herder clashes affect both Christians and Muslims. The government has noted it was implementing security reforms, engaging with US on fact-finding, and strengtheni

item.title: Power sector fix ‘ongoing work’ — APC-PCC; bonds can’t light homes, says ADC-PCC
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi & Luminous Jannamike ABUJA—The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council, APC-PCC, and African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, were yesterday locked in a verbal war over President Bola Tinubu’s declaration during his campaign in 2023 that if he failed to give Nigerians power, they should not re-elect him in 2027. Read Also: Banks raise lending rates for top borrowers despite CBN cuts While APC-PCC said the President’s fixing of the country’s electricity sector was ongoing and had signed the Electricity Act 2023 to enable states generate, distribute and transmit power, ADC-PCC insisted Nigerians could not power their homes and businesses with laws, bonds and project announcements. In a statement yesterday, the spokesperson of APC-PCC, Dele Alake, said recent public commentary had reproduced the campaign promise without its closing qualification. Speaking to members of the Organised Private Sector, OPS, in Lagos, ahead of the 2023 general elections, Tinubu, then the APC candidate, had reportedly said: “Whichever way, by all means necessary, you will have electricity, and you will not pay for estimated bills anymore. ‘’A promise made will be a promise kept. If I don’t keep the promise and I come for a second term, don’t vote for me, unless I give you adequate reasons I couldn’t deliver.” Alake said the commentary left out the final part, that “should he fall short, he would owe Nigerians an adequate explanation before seeking their support for a second term.” He argued that a fair assessment of the pledge should consider the full statement, alongside the administration’s record since 2023, measured against measurable improvements in electricity supply, metering, infrastructure and market stability. “While fixing the power sector crisis remains unfinished, the President is working consistently to deliver on his promise to Nigerians, and his commitment to face the challenges head-on has never diminished,” the council said. The APC-PCC said Tinubu signed the Electricity Act, 2023, on June 9, within two weeks of taking office. According to the council, the law liberalised and deregulated the power sector and moved it away from the Exclusive List, so states can take part in power generation, distribution and transmission. It said Lagos, Enugu, Abia, Ekiti, Oyo, Kaduna and Niger states had started using the law to set up their own electricity regulatory agencies and attract private capital. On debts, the campaign council said Tinubu “took on the over N6 trillion legacy debt that had accumulated from 2015 to 2025,” adding that the administration created a N4 trillion bond programme to settle verified legacy debts owed 21 power generation companies, Gencos, and gas companies, Gascos. The council said the first and second tranches of the programme had raised over N1.2 trillion, and noted that the effect was becoming evident in the ability of Gencos to invest in upgrading their plants. “Just a few days

item.title: India floats AI plan under which ‘The model travels to the data, rather than the data travelling to the model’
item.description: As debate and legal argument continue over the extent to which developers of large language models are entitled to feed the world’s data into their systems without paying for it, India’s government has come up with an idea to regulate and secure the flow of information. India’s motive is to create AI models trained on local data, because it thinks offshore model-makers won’t be motivated to address the nation’s issues or to ensure owners of data stay in control. The scheme India’s Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) thinks can make that happen is called the “Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture (DEPA) for AI Training.” As described by Professor Ajay Kumar Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, DEPA means “the model travels to the data, rather than the data travelling to the model.” The scheme envisions “Training Data Providers” (TDPs) – examples of which include hospitals, banks, and government agencies – sharing anonymized and encrypted data with a “Data Exchange Platform” (DEP). Entities called “Training Data Consumers” (TDCs) access the data stored at the DEPs to train their models. DEPs will operate what MeitY calls “hardware-based Secure Data Environments” in which “data remains encrypted and isolated even during processing.” They also enforce rules set by TDPs that describe how TDCs can use data. MeitY’s DEPA framework [PDF] says this scheme means “Differential privacy techniques are systematically applied to prevent the model from learning or revealing individual specific information,” adding “All activities inside the secure data environments are immutably logged for audit purposes, ensuring that the process is both secure and transparent.” India’s government already operates several data exchanges, but it is unclear how much work remains to make DEPA a reality. Once DEPA is working, MeitY envisions model-makers will use it to do things like “unlock currently fragmented health data to power breakthroughs in AI-driven diagnostics, drug discovery, and public health management.” The optimism extends to financial services. India is home to literally thousands of banks, and MeitY thinks “DEPA can enable secure sharing of diverse financial data, potentially extending formal credit to 400 million underserved individuals and MSMEs and fueling next-generation fintech innovation.” India’s government has long believed that if financial services companies can lend to more people, it will boost economic development. “Similarly, in Education, DEPA can overcome data interoperability challenges to enable AI-powered personalized learning for millions and create portable skill credentials essential for a future-ready workforce of its 250 million students in a $29 billion EdTech sector,” the framework states. “The successful adoption of DEPA Training across these domains is the essential catalyst for realizing India’s vision of inclusive growth and responsible AI leadership on the global stage.” While t

item.title: N70,000 allowance showdown: Civil servants fire back at TUC
item.description: *Insist FG-Labour agreement stands *JNPSNC reveals details of agreement, including 6-month transport allowance, others By Victor Ahiuma-Young Civil servants, under the aegis of Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council, JNPSNC, have defended the N70,000 transportation allowance agreement reached between the federal government and organised labour, insisting that the rejection of the deal by the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria, TUC, would not affect its implementation. Read Also: TUC rejects FG’s proposed N70,000 monthly transport allowance for workers The council said the agreement, signed on October 27, 2026, followed more than six hours of intensive negotiations and constructive engagements involving the federal government, the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, JNPSNC and the Joint Health Sector Unions JOHESU. The position of the council was contained in a circular signed by the National Secretary, Mr Gbenga Olowoyo, and addressed to the national presidents and general secretaries of affiliated unions, as well as state chairmen and secretaries of the Joint Public Service Negotiating Councils across the federation. The unions JNPSNC is made up of the Association of Senior Civil Servants of Nigeria, ASCSN; Nigeria Civil Service Union, NCSU; Nigeria Union of Public Service, Reportorial, Secretarial, Data Processors and Allied Workers, NUPSTRAW; Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria, MHWUN; and National Association of Nigeria Nurses and Midwives, NANNM. Others are Nigeria Union of Agriculture and Allied Employees, NUAAE; Amalgamated Union of Public Corporations; Civil Service Technical and Recreational Services Employees, AUPCTRE; and National Union of Printing, Publishing and Paper Products Workers, NUPPPPROW. On the government side are the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment; Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation; Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation; Federal Ministry of Justice; Federal Civil Service Commission; National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission; Federal Ministry of Finance; Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation; and Budget Office of the Federation. In the circular, Olowoyo explained that the N70,000 transportation allowance would be paid monthly to public servants for six months, beginning from November 2026, to cushion the impact of rising transportation costs on workers and their dependents. He also urged state and local governments to embrace the agreement and complement the federal government’s intervention, particularly in view of the substantial revenue accruing to the sub-national governments. The circular read, among others: “The meeting was not only tough but also took more than six hours before both the Federal Government and labour sides could enter into terms. “On the issue of payment of N70,000 transportation allowance, which will be paid for the next six months to public servants, starting from the month of November 2026, it was meant to subsidis

According to analysts, although the market’s upward movement suggests renewed investor confidence, the uneven distribution of gains points to a selective investment strategy. This divergence between index performance and market breadth remains an important consideration in assessing the sustainability of the current rally. On the global market, the oil prices continued to record performance as the retreat in prices last week reflected a reassessment of geopolitical risks as diplomatic efforts sought to revive peace negotiations. However, analysts noted that the outlook for oil remains sensitive to developments in the region, and renewed escalation could quickly alter market expectations. For Nigeria, movements in crude oil prices have implications for government revenue, foreign exchange supply and broader economic expectations. Higher oil prices can support public revenue and external balances, although their overall effect depends on production levels, domestic fuel costs and other economic conditions. item.title: Fresh woes for pupils in Niger
item.description: At least 12 pupils of Madarasatul Nurul Islam, Maikujeri community in Rafi Local Government Area of Niger State have been reportedly kidnapped by bandits. Daily Trust gathered that the children were abducted around 10am on Saturday while harvesting maize on their teacher’s farm on the outskirts of the town. A resident, Mohammed Adamu, told Daily Trust that the children were already on their way home when the bandits struck and picked them. An Okada man identified as Tasi’u, who attempted to escape, was reportedly shot and is currently receiving treatment at the IBB Specialist Hospital in Minna, the state capital. How bureaucracy leaves power equipment rotting in ports Sokoto: Concerns over attack on ADC guber candidate’s convoy Another source close to the Quranic school told one of our correspondents that 13 people, including 12 female pupils of the school and the younger brother of the school’s proprietor, Mallam Mainasara, were kidnapped. He said the victims, aged between nine and 14, were abducted as they stopped by a borehole to wash themselves and drink water after leaving the farm. According to him, the pupils had been working on the farm with their teacher when the teacher received information that bandits were advancing towards the area. He said the teacher immediately instructed the pupils to return home while he also left on his motorcycle. “While on their way home, the pupils reportedly stopped at a borehole to wash their bodies and drink water. It was at that point that the armed men swooped on them and whisked them away,” he said. The source further disclosed that some women were also abducted from another farm in the area. When contacted, the spokesperson for the Niger Police Command, SP Wasiu Abiodun, promised to verify the information and revert. The police spokesperson, however, revealed that six people were rescued but was silent on the abduction of the pupils. He said, “On 29th October, 2026, at about 12.30pm, joint security tactical teams during a clearance and rescue operation around Pandogari Rafi LGA rescued six abducted victims who were reportedly kidnapped by some hoodlums on 28th October, 2026 at about 12 pm in their farms at Mahangi village via Pandogari. “The victims were abducted and taken to Hanawanka forest where they were rescued unhurt. They were later received at Kagara Div for debriefing and medical attention ahead of reunion with their relatives.” Map of Niger State with red cycle indicating the LGA where the incident took place Dozens of farmers displaced Similarly, dozens of farming communities in Borgu, Mariga, Mashegu and Rijau LGAs have continued to flee their homes following the renewed bandits’ attacks. The affected farmers told Daily Trust that their farm produce, including rice, soyabeans and maize, is wasting on their farms because bandits have stopped them from harvesting. item.title: Google says Asian advertisers spending less due to Europe's customs changes
item.description: Google has revealed some of its Asian customers – almost certainly Chinese e-tailers – are buying fewer ads. Speaking on Alphabet’s Q3 earnings call last week, chief business officer Philipp Schindler addressed the slowdown in ad sales growth with the following remark: “In retail, some of our APAC advertisers were impacted by the EU eliminating its de minimis exemption.” That’s a reference to the European Union’s changes to import duties, which saw the bloc introduce a temporary €3 customs duty for every consignment valued at under €150 imported from outside the EU. The EU previously operated the de minimis exemption that Schindler referred to, meaning it collected no import duty on almost 5.9 billion low-value items shipped to the continent in 2025 alone. The new regime aims to protect European retailers from cheap imports. A great many of those items came from Chinese e-tail giants – the likes of Temu, Shein, and Alibaba – who are thought to account for perhaps ten percent of advertising revenue at Google and Meta. EU policy has therefore contributed to slower growth at Google. Huawei’s brake pedals reportedly break Huawei’s automotive efforts appear to have driven it into a cul de sac of controversy. The Chinese tech giant works with a company called Anhui Jianghuai Automobile Group Co. (JAC) under the Harmony Intelligent Mobility Alliance , which aims to produce intelligent cars. The flagship model produced by Huawei and JAC is a luxury EV called the Maextro V800, which when tested by Chinese automotive review site Dongchedi produced a rather terrifying fault: the brake pedal bracket broke when drivers exerted maximum force during tests to assess the car's ability to decelerate suddenly at 100 km/h. The site’s drivers were still able to stop the car, but rather more slowly than is optimal. Within days of the review site posting its findings, reports of its work started to disappear from the internet, according to China Digital Times , a US-based outlet that says it publishes independent news on Chinese affairs. Even some opinion pieces that called for further assessment of the car’s safety disappeared, giving rise to theories that Beijing is displeased with negative coverage of its technology champions and automotive industry. North Korea named as Binance hacker The USA’s Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) on Saturday named North Korea’s elite cybercrime crew “TraderTraitor” as the source of last week’s attack on cryptocurrency exchange Binance . Cyber-defense company TRM also reached the same conclusion. Its analysts last week declared they have “high confidence” that “on and off-chain intelligence” suggest TraderTraitor did the deed. “On the evening of October 29, billions of dollars in crypto began leaving wallets belonging to Binance,” TRM’s analysts wrote. “Within minutes, Binance wallets on the XRP Ledger, Ethereum, Bitcoin, Tron, Solana and four other networks had sent their balances to addresses controlled by a single attacker. item.description: There was a time in the distant past when good things could occasionally come out of Twitter. Back in 2017, novelists Sam Sykes (the Aeons’ Gate series) and Chuck Wendig ( Blackbirds, Star Wars: Aftermath ) got on the website currently known as X to co-write an improvised horror satire . The result was a firmly tongue-in-cheek deconstruction of slasher movies, concerning Sykes' unnamed character’s new job as a camp counselor and an unfolding massacre in the woods. The story quickly went viral. (While the tweets are still up, Wendig has since abandoned X and locked his account, so the original story can no longer be read outside of a handful of unofficial screenshot archives.)
